name: Wheel of Heaven Translation Glossary — Genesis WoH overlay
description: Per-translation overlay for the Genesis WoH translation. Records lexical decisions that are text-specific (toponyms, hapax legomena, single-chapter aetiologies, chapter-keystone interpretive cruxes) and would bloat the central glossary if promoted. Promotion to the central glossary is an editorial-judgment call as future books are translated and lemmas recur. Pinned to the central `translation-glossary.json` v2.46.0 as of 2026-05-31.
scopeNote:

Added (overlay): (i) `patriarchal-beer-sheva-cross-cycle-node-gen46` (v 1) — Be'er-Sheva as the cross-patriarchal-stopping-point (Gen 21:33 Avraham planting the eshel; Gen 26:23-25 Yitzchaq's altar and theophany; Gen 28:10 Ya'aqov's departure; Gen 46:1 Ya'aqov's final-departure); the literary-observation as a node-of-the-cycle documented; promotion-seed for the prophetic Be'er-Sheva-pilgrimage-shrine indictments (1 Sam 8, Amos 5:5, 8:14). (iii) `ha-el-divine-name-with-definite-article-gen46` (v 3) — the *ha-El* form (relatively rare definite-articled El divine-name); cross-corpus Gen 31:13, 35:1, 35:3, Ps 18:31+33, 2 Sam 22:31+33, Job 8:3, 22:13, Isa 42:5; distinguished from the simple *El* (anarthrous) and from *Elohim*. (iv) `yashit-yado-al-eineikha-close-eyes-at-death-formula-gen46` (v 4) — the chapter-singular close-the-eyes-at-death formula in the deity's promise to Ya'aqov. (v) `taph-little-ones-dependents-class-yosef-cycle-gen46` (v 5) — the *taph* dependents-class noun ('little ones'); corpus-saturating cross-corpus reach into Exodus / Numbers / Deuteronomy / Joshua / Judges; promotion-seed for Exodus translation. (vi) `miqneh-rekhush-patriarchal-mobile-wealth-formula-gen46` (v 6) — the *miqneh* + *rekhush* pair as the patriarchal-mobile-wealth-formula; cross-corpus Gen 12:5, 13:6, 31:18, 36:6, 7. (vii) `ben-ha-kenaanit-shimon-canaanitess-son-gen46` (v 10) — Sha'ul ben ha-Kena'anit as the only mother-ethnicity-qualifier in the seventy-souls list; cross-corpus Exod 6:15; chapter-internal literary-observation. (viii) `er-onan-died-in-kenaan-gen38-back-reference-gen46` (v 12) — the genealogy's only narrative-historical aside, the Gen 38:7-10 back-reference; SIBLING overlay-entry to the existing overlay `ve-shichet-artzah-onan-euphemism` (Gen 38:9) with bidirectional cross-reference. (ix) `yov-yashuv-ketiv-qere-yissachar-textual-variant-gen46` (v 13) — the *Yov* (MT) / *Yashuv* (Sam, LXX, Num 26:24, 1 Chr 7:1) textual-critical variant. (x) `binyamin-sons-list-textual-crux-gen46` (v 21) — MAJOR. The ten-sons list vs Num 26:38-40 (five sons with Ard and Na'aman becoming Bela's grandsons) vs 1 Chr 7:6 (three sons) vs 1 Chr 8:1-2 (five sons); the documentary-critical reading (Wellhausen, Skinner, Friedman) AND the harmonizing reading (Cassuto, Hamilton) documented even-handedly; the v 21 *Rosh* singular-attestation and the name-form variants (Echi/Achiram; Muppim/Shefufam; Chuppim/Chufam) documented WITHOUT adjudication. (xvii) `amutah-ha-paam-death-readiness-yaaqov-gen46` (v 30) — the cohortative + emphatic *ha-pa'am* in Ya'aqov's death-readiness statement; SIBLING overlay-entry to the existing `va-techi-ruach-yaaqov-spirit-revival-chayah-arc-gen45` (the chapter-45 spirit-revival arc) with bidirectional cross-reference; the Gen 45:28 → 46:30 cycle's death-readiness arc closure documented. (xviii) `yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-cycle-wide-pattern-gen46` (vv 1, 2, 5) — the chapter-46 continuation of the cycle-wide Ya'aqov/Yisra'el name-shift pattern; SIBLING overlay-entry to the existing `yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-yosef-cycle-acceptance-v28` (Gen 45:28); the chapter-internal Yisra'el (v 1, v 2a, v 5b *bnei Yisra'el*) / Ya'aqov (v 2b doubled-call, v 2c, v 5a, v 8) alternation as the chapter's continuation of the cycle-wide pattern documented; the cycle-wide central-candidate flagged for future processing (Gen 46-50 cluster). Extended appliesTo (overlay): `paddan-aram-binyamin-contradiction-documentary-seam` += GEN-WOH-46:15 (the Le'ah-list's Paddan-Aram-formula at Gen 46:15 — Le'ah's sons WERE all born in Paddan-Aram and Dinah is named here as born there too; the broader source-critical observation extends, with the chapter-46 entry's rationale noting that the Binyamin-contradiction itself does NOT surface here directly); `va-yippol-al-tzavarav-reunion-embrace-formula-gen45` += GEN-WOH-46:29 (the third member of the Genesis-internal reunion-embrace formula cluster Gen 33:4 + 45:14-15 + 46:29; the entry's existing rationale already names Gen 46:29 explicitly); `agalot-pharaoh-issue-wagons-yosef-cycle-gen45` += GEN-WOH-46:5 (the chapter's continuation of the wagons-cycle from the Gen 45 grant; the wagons issued at Gen 45:19, 21, 27 are here used at Gen 46:5 to transport the family — the entry's existing rationale already documents the narrative-trajectory from the grant to the use). Extended rationale (overlay): `ve-shichet-artzah-onan-euphemism` (Gen 38:9) — extended with a 'Cross-reference (the Gen 46:12 Er-Onan back-reference sibling-overlay link)' paragraph naming the new `er-onan-died-in-kenaan-gen38-back-reference-gen46` sibling by id; `va-techi-ruach-yaaqov-spirit-revival-chayah-arc-gen45` (Gen 45:27) — extended with a 'Cross-reference (the Gen 46:30 *amutah ha-pa'am* sibling-overlay link)' paragraph naming the new `amutah-ha-paam-death-readiness-yaaqov-gen46` sibling by id and documenting the cycle's death-readiness arc (Gen 45:28 → 46:30); `yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-yosef-cycle-acceptance-v28` (Gen 45:28) — extended with a 'Cross-reference (the Gen 46:1-2-5 name-shift sibling-overlay link)' paragraph naming the new `yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-cycle-wide-pattern-gen46` sibling by id. **v1.13.0 (Genesis 45) adds sixteen overlay entries from the disclosure chapter — Yosef's *hitvadda* self-disclosure (the recognition-arc inversion), the brothers' *nivhal*-dismay, the cycle's *makhar*-sale verbal-naming, the emotional-discharge pair, the Pharaonic court-advisor title, the sustenance-promise, the direct-speech reversal of the Gen 42 interpreter, the court-honor *kavod*, the reunion-embrace formula, the *chelev*-of-the-land idiom, the Pharaoh-wagons, the chapter's *chamesh*-fives pattern, the *al-tirgezu* philological crux, the rare *va-yafag* faint-heart hapax, the chayah-arc closure at v 27, and the Ya'aqov→Yisra'el name-shift at v 28 — and extends one existing overlay entry's appliesTo (`yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim` += GEN-WOH-45:5, 7, 8, 9 — the chapter's four Elohim-occurrences, the cycle's most-concentrated single-chapter Elohim-cluster after Gen 41).** Added (overlay): (i) `hitvadda-yosef-self-disclosure-recognition-pair-gen45` (v 1) — Yosef's marked Hithpael of *yada* in the self-disclosure register; SIBLING overlay-entry to the existing overlay `nakar-hitnakker-recognition-feigning-gen42` (the Gen 42:7 Hithpael of *nakar*, 'made himself strange') with bidirectional cross-reference; the chapter-45 *hitvadda* (recognition-disclosed) is the explicit literary inverse of the chapter-42 *hitnakker* (recognition-withheld); the cycle's Hithpael-pair structure documented; ASV-baseline 'made himself known' retained. (ii) `nivhalu-mi-panav-brothers-dismay-disclosure-scene-gen45` (v 3) — the Niphal of *bahal* 'be terrified, dismayed' in the brothers' speechlessness at the disclosure; chapter-singular within Genesis (the lexeme's only Genesis occurrence); the structural-inverse of Yehudah's just-completed Gen 44 surety-speech (the speaker becomes the speechless); ASV-baseline 'dismayed at his presence'. (iii) `mekhartem-oti-brothers-sale-yosef-cycle-arc` (vv 4, 5) — Yosef's verbal-naming of the Gen 37 sale (*mekhartem oti Mitzraymah* at v 4; *ki mekhartem oti hennah* at v 5); the cycle-internal Gen 37:27, 28, 36 → Gen 45:4-5 *makhar*-arc as the cycle's moral-keyword; ASV-baseline 'sold'. (iv) `al-teatzevu-veal-yichar-emotional-discharge-pair-gen45` (v 5) — Yosef's emotional-discharge instruction *al-tea'tzevu ve-al-yichar be-eineikhem*; the *atzav* root cross-Genesis echo to Gen 3:16-17 (the woman's and the ground's *itzavon*), Gen 5:29 (Lemekh's naming of Noach), Gen 6:6 (YHWH's *va-yit'atzev*); chapter-specific instruction-pair; ASV-baseline 'be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves'. (v) `av-le-paroh-court-advisor-title-egyptological-gen45` (v 8) — the *av le-Par'oh* office-title (Egyptian-court 'father' for senior advisor / vizier); cross-corpus parallels 2 Chr 2:13 (Huram-Abi), Isa 22:21 (Elyaqim), Job 29:16 (Iyov as father-to-the-needy); Egyptological apparatus Vergote, Redford, Kitchen; ASV-baseline 'a father to Pharaoh'. (vi) `kalkel-yosef-sustenance-promise-gen45-46-47-50` (v 11) — Yosef's *ve-khilkalti otkha sham* sustenance-promise; the cycle's three-fold *kalkel*-arc Gen 45:11 + 47:12 + 50:21 documented; cross-corpus reach into 2 Sam 19, 1 Kgs 17-18, etc. noted as promotion-seed; ASV-baseline 'I will nourish thee'. (vii) `fi-ha-medabber-aleikhem-direct-speech-reversal-melitz-gen45` (v 12) — Yosef's *ki fi ha-medabber aleikhem* ('it is my mouth that speaketh unto you'); SIBLING overlay-entry to the existing overlay `melitz-interpreter-rare-sense-gen42` (the Gen 42:23 interpreter-mediation) with bidirectional cross-reference; the cycle's mediated-speech / direct-speech literary reversal documented; ASV-baseline 'my mouth that speaketh unto you'. (viii) `kavod-court-office-honor-yosef-egyptian-glory-gen45` (v 13) — the *kavod* in the court-office-honor register; distinct from the divine-glory-of-YHWH cluster; cross-corpus parallels Esth 1:4 + 5:11 (Pharaoh's / Haman's court-honor *kavod*); ASV-baseline 'all my glory'. (ix) `va-yippol-al-tzavarav-reunion-embrace-formula-gen45` (vv 14, 15) — the *va-yippol al tzavarav + va-yevk* reunion-embrace-and-weeping formula; Gen 33:4 (Esav's reunion-embrace with Ya'aqov) + Gen 45:14-15 (Yosef-Binyamin / Yosef-brothers embrace) + Gen 46:29 (Yosef-Ya'aqov embrace) cycle-triplet; named scholarship literary observation (Alter, Sternberg, Sarna). ASV-baseline 'fell upon his neck and wept'. (x) `chelev-ha-aretz-best-of-the-land-pharaoh-grant-gen45` (v 18) — the *chelev* in the metaphorical 'best of' register; cross-corpus Num 18:12, Deut 32:14, Ps 81:17 + 147:14; distinguished from the Levitical sacrificial-fat prohibition-register; ASV-baseline 'the fat of the land'. (xi) `agalot-pharaoh-issue-wagons-yosef-cycle-gen45` (vv 19, 21, 27) — the chapter's three-fold *agalot* deployment for Pharaoh-issue wagons; cross-corpus Num 7:3 + 6-8 (the Mishkan-transport), 1 Sam 6:7-14 (the ark-transport), 2 Sam 6:3, Isa 5:18, Amos 2:13; Egyptological apparatus Vergote, Redford; ASV-baseline 'wagons'. (xii) `chamesh-chalifot-semalot-fives-pattern-gen45` (v 22) — the *chamesh chalifot semalot* gift to Binyamin; the cycle-wide 'fives'-pattern (Gen 41:34 *chimmesh* / 43:34 *chamesh-yadot* / 45:6 + 11 *chamesh shanim* / 45:22 *chamesh chalifot* / 47:2 *chamesh anashim*) documented as the cycle's numerical-keyword; the *chalifot semalot* gift-formula cross-corpus parallels (Judg 14:12-19; 2 Kgs 5) noted; ASV-baseline 'five changes of raiment'. (xiii) `al-tirgezu-ba-derekh-philological-crux-gen45` (v 24) — Yosef's farewell instruction *al tirgezu ba-derekh*; the tannaitic / medieval philological-crux (b. Ta'an. 10b, Rashi, Targum Onqelos, Saadia); four readings (trembling-anxiety / quarreling / agitated-travel / fear) documented; ASV-baseline 'see that ye fall not out by the way' (the quarrel-reading, the dominant Jewish-tradition + KJV/ASV consensus). (xiv) `va-yafag-libbo-heart-grew-numb-rare-form-gen45` (v 26) — the rare Qal of *pug* 'grow numb, faint, cease'; the lexeme's chapter-singular hapax within Genesis (the only other Qal-stem occurrence at Ps 77:3 in the *ne'enachti* parallel-stich, and Hab 1:4 Hiphil); the marked-rare-form for Ya'aqov's emotional-collapse on hearing the impossible news; ASV-baseline 'his heart fainted'. (xv) `va-techi-ruach-yaaqov-spirit-revival-chayah-arc-gen45` (v 27) — the chapter-closing *va-techi ruach Ya'aqov* spirit-revival; SIBLING overlay-entry to the central `michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun` (the providential-purpose-noun of v 5); the chapter's chayah-keyword arc (v 5 *le-michyah* + v 7 *u-le-hachayot* + v 27 *va-techi ruach Ya'aqov*) — providential-purpose → expanded-purpose → fulfilment-in-the-father — documented; cross-corpus chayah-of-spirit-revival parallels Judg 15:19, 1 Sam 30:12; ASV-baseline 'the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived'. (xvi) `yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-yosef-cycle-acceptance-v28` (v 28) — the chapter's narrative-pivot from Ya'aqov (vv 25, 27 twice) to Yisra'el (v 28); the named-shift at the patriarch's acceptance-of-the-news / determination-to-go; the literary-and-source-critical observation (Sarna, Alter, von Rad, Brueggemann); the cross-cycle parallel name-shifts at Gen 46:1-2 + 47:27-31 + 48:2 + 49:1-2 noted; ASV-baseline 'and Yisra'el said' (the source's name preserved). Extended appliesTo (scope-formalization): `yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim` += GEN-WOH-45:5, 7, 8, 9 — the chapter's four Elohim-occurrences (v 5 *shelachani Elohim*; v 7 *va-yishlacheni Elohim*; v 8 *ha-Elohim*, with definite article; v 9 *samani Elohim*); the cycle's most-concentrated single-chapter Elohim-cluster after Gen 41; the providential-sending formula (at vv 5, 7, 8) governed centrally by `shelachani-elohim-lifneikhem-providential-sending-formula-yosef-cycle`. Extended rationale (scope-formalization): `nakar-hitnakker-recognition-feigning-gen42` — extended with a 'Cross-reference (the Gen 45:1 *hitvadda* sibling-overlay link)' paragraph naming the new `hitvadda-yosef-self-disclosure-recognition-pair-gen45` sibling by id and documenting the recognition-arc Hithpael-pair (hitnakker recognition-withheld at Gen 42:7 ↔ hitvadda recognition-disclosed at Gen 45:1); `melitz-interpreter-rare-sense-gen42` — extended with a 'Cross-reference (the Gen 45:12 *fi ha-medabber* sibling-overlay link)' paragraph naming the new `fi-ha-medabber-aleikhem-direct-speech-reversal-melitz-gen45` sibling by id and documenting the cycle's mediated-speech / direct-speech literary reversal (Gen 42:23 interpreter-mediation ↔ Gen 45:12 Yosef-mouth-directly). No WoH synthesis on the surface or in any rationale; the translation surface stays ASV-baseline 1901 with WoH proper-name transliteration. **v1.12.0 (Genesis 44) adds eight overlay entries from the silver-cup chapter — the moral climax of the Yosef cycle, Yehudah's great substitution-speech, the third *hishtachavah*-fulfilment — and extends seven existing overlay entries' appliesTo (scope-formalization).** Added (overlay): (i) `nitztaddaq-hithpael-tzadaq-yehudah-arc-gen44` (v 16) — Yehudah's *mah-nitztaddaq* ('how shall we clear ourselves') — the rare Hithpael of *tzadaq* in the reflexive-declarative 'declare-oneself-righteous / clear-oneself' sense; SIBLING overlay-entry to the existing overlay `tzadqah-mimmeni-she-is-in-the-right` (Gen 38:26, Yehudah's first *tzadaq* moment, the Tamar-vindication) with bidirectional cross-reference; the Yehudah-internal Gen 38:26 → Gen 44:16 *tzadaq*-arc (the man who once declared Tamar *tzadqah mimmeni* now declares his brothers' inability to *nitztaddaq*) documented as the project's third overlay-overlay sibling pair (Gen 37↔38 *haker-na*, Gen 38↔43 *arav-eravon*, Gen 38↔44 *tzadaq*); ASV-baseline 'how shall we clear ourselves' retained. (ii) `self-curse-oath-formula-vamet-gen44` (v 9) — the brothers' over-broad self-imprecation *asher yimmatze ito me-avadekha va-met ve-gam-anachnu nihyeh la-adoni la-avadim* ('with whomsoever it be found, let him die, and we also will be my lord's bondmen'); the documented Genesis-internal echo to Gen 31:32 (Ya'aqov's unwitting *lo yichyeh* self-curse on Rachel, who has Lavan's *terafim*); both involve a missing precious-object hidden in the youngest-Rachel-line member's possessions; both invoke a death-curse that the speaker does not realize will boomerang; ASV-baseline 'let him die, and we also will be my lord's bondmen'. (iii) `qara-simlot-rent-garments-grief-formula-yosef-cycle` (v 13) — the Yosef-cycle grief-formula triplet *qara begadim/simlot* across Gen 37:29 (Re'uven at the empty pit, the cycle's first grief-rending) → 37:34 (Ya'aqov on receiving the bloodied tunic) → 44:13 (the ten brothers as collective-subject); the corpus-wide grief-rending lexeme noted for promotion-seed (Num 14:6, Josh 7:6, Judg 11:35, 2 Sam 1:11; 3:31; 13:31, 1 Kgs 21:27, 2 Kgs 2:12; 5:7; 6:30; 11:14; 18:37; 19:1; 22:11 + 19, Esth 4:1, Job 1:20; 2:12, Jer 36:24, Joel 2:13); ASV-baseline 'they rent their clothes'. (iv) `tarof-toraf-paronomastic-torn-in-pieces-yaaqov-belief-gen37-44` (v 28) — the paronomastic infinitive-absolute + finite verb of *taraf* 'to tear (by a wild beast)' in Ya'aqov's reported-by-Yehudah repetition of Gen 37:33's *tarof toraf Yosef*; the lexical-verbatim cross-chapter echo locks Ya'aqov's continued belief in the Gen 37 false-evidence; SIBLING overlay-entry to the existing `chayah-raah-evil-or-wild-beast` (Gen 37:20, 33) with bidirectional cross-reference; the cross-corpus *taraf* distribution (Exod 22:12, Jer 5:6, Hos 5:14, 6:1, 13:8, Mic 5:8, Nah 2:13, Ps 7:3, 17:12, 22:14, 50:22) noted; ASV-baseline 'surely he is torn in pieces'. (v) `search-by-birth-order-eldest-youngest-gen44` (v 12) — the literary marker *ba-gadol hechel u-va-qaton killah* ('began at the eldest, and left off at the youngest'); the merism *eldest→youngest* as a Yosef-cycle birth-order-as-literary-structure marker, paired with the Gen 43:33 seating-order observation (the cycle's persistent foregrounding of birth-order); ASV-baseline 'began at the eldest, and left off at the youngest'. (vi) `shenayim-yaledah-li-ishti-rachel-exclusive-wife-gen44` (v 27) — Ya'aqov's marked phrasing (reported by Yehudah) *shenayim yaledah-li ishti* ('my wife bare me two sons'); the literary marker of Ya'aqov's enduring Rachel-centric grief — Le'ah, Bilhah, and Zilpah excluded from the *ishti* designation; the ten elder brothers excluded from the *yaledah-li shenayim* count; documented across standard commentary (Sarna, Westermann, Alter); ASV-baseline 'my wife bare me two sons' literal preserved. terms.translit: Machanayim
terms.partOfSpeech: proper noun (dual-form of *machaneh*, *camp*)
terms.literal: two camps / double-camp / camp-pair
terms.standardEnglish: Mahanaim (ASV/KJV/NRSV/NJPS — transliterated, no in-text gloss)
terms.wohChoice: Machanayim (transliterated, matching WoH place-name convention; the dual-form etymology surfaced in commentary)
terms.rationale:
**Gen 32:2-3 (MT) records Ya'aqov's encounter with the *mal'akhei Elohim* (messengers of Elohim) and his renaming of the place as *Machanayim* — a dual-form of *machaneh* (camp). The toponym's in-text etymology (*machaneh Elohim zeh* — *this is Elohim's camp*, v 3) and the chapter's later *shnei machanot* (two camps, vv 8-9) frame the toponym ambiguously between two readings: (a) the dual as a true dual (Ya'aqov's camp + the divine messenger-camp); (b) the dual as a reference to Ya'aqov's later self-divided two-camps strategy.**

**The dual-form *machanayim*.** Hebrew nouns can take three numbers: singular, plural, and dual. The dual-form is reserved for paired-objects (body-parts that come in pairs: *yadayim* / hands, *raglayim* / feet, *einayim* / eyes; pairs of objects: *yomayim* / two days, *p'amayim* / two times). The dual-form of *machaneh* (camp) produces *machanayim* — *two camps*. The form is grammatically a dual, not a plural — the plural would be *machanot* (which appears at vv 8, 9, 11). The chapter's deliberate alternation between *machanayim* (the dual, used as the place-name at v 3 and absent elsewhere) and *machanot* (the plural, used at vv 8, 9, 11 for Ya'aqov's strategy) is editorially-significant: the toponym preserves the dual specifically.

**The two-reading ambiguity.** Modern critical scholarship identifies two readings of the toponym's dual-reference:

*(i) The divine-camp + Ya'aqov's-camp reading.* At v 3 Ya'aqov sees the *mal'akhei Elohim* and exclaims *machaneh Elohim zeh* (*this is Elohim's camp*). The toponym *Machanayim* would then refer to the two camps present at the site: the divine messenger-camp + Ya'aqov's traveling-camp. The reading is favored by **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 224 (the divine and human camps meeting at the site); **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 506-507; **von Rad** *Genesis* OTL 1972 p. 315. The reading sits comfortably with the inclusio reading of Gen 28:12 / 32:2 — the outbound Bethel-ladder vision and the inbound Machanayim-encounter both feature *mal'akhei Elohim*, framing Ya'aqov's twenty-year-flight-and-return between two divine-messenger encounters.

*(ii) The Ya'aqov's-two-self-divided-camps reading.* The chapter's later narrative (vv 8-9, 11) records Ya'aqov dividing his people into *shnei machanot* (two camps) as protection against Esav. On this reading, the toponym *Machanayim* foreshadows or aetiologizes the two-camp division. The reading is favored by **Hamilton** *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 p. 321 (the toponym anticipates the two-camp strategy) and by some midrashic traditions (Genesis Rabbah 75:9). The reading explains the dual-form by reference to the chapter's later narrative-development.

*(iii) The toponym-as-locative reading.* A minority reading: the dual-ending *-ayim* is the toponym's locative-or-genuine-dual marker (cf. *Mitzrayim* — Egypt — whose dual-form has been variously read as a genuine dual referring to Upper and Lower Egypt or as a locative-pluralizing ending). On this reading the toponym is opaque to interpretation and the in-text etymology is a post-facto folk-etymology. The reading is treated by **Sarna** p. 224 and rejected.

**The cross-corpus *Machanayim* distribution.** The toponym recurs across the HB at: **Josh 13:26, 30** (the Gad-and-half-tribe-of-Manasseh territorial allocation — *Machanayim* in the Gad / Reuben territorial-list); **Josh 21:38** (the Levitical-cities list — *Machanayim* as a Merarite Levitical-city); **2 Sam 2:8-12** (Avner takes Ish-Bosheth to *Machanayim* and makes it the Sha'ulide capital after the death of Sha'ul); **2 Sam 17:24, 27; 19:33; 1 Kgs 2:8** (David flees to *Machanayim* during the Avshalom-rebellion, and the *Machanayim* trans-Jordanian region is the base of David's loyal supporters Barzillai, Shovi, and Makhir); **1 Kgs 4:14** (Achinadav son of Iddo at *Machanayim* — one of Shlomo's twelve administrative-district officers); **Song 6:13 [MT 7:1]** (*ki-mecholat ha-machanayim* — *as the dance of the two-camps* — the only non-toponym occurrence of the dual-form, used metaphorically). The cross-corpus distribution places *Machanayim* in the trans-Jordan region (consistent with the Gen 32 setting at the Yabboq) and confirms its historical-geographical existence as an Iron Age Israelite settlement.

**The Bethel-Machanayim inclusio.** The chapter's wider editorial structure positions Machanayim as the inbound-counterpart to Gen 28:12's outbound Bethel-ladder vision. The verbal echo: Gen 28:12 *mal'akhei Elohim olim v-yordim bo* (the plural-messenger image); Gen 32:2 *va-yifge'u vo mal'akhei Elohim* (the messengers meeting Ya'aqov). The two verses are the only HB occurrences of plural-form *mal'akhei Elohim* in narrative-mode (the formula recurs elsewhere only in non-narrative contexts; see the central-glossary entry [malakhei-elohim-ascending-descending](#malakhei-elohim-ascending-descending) for Gen 28:12). The Machanayim-encounter at v 2 thus brackets the twenty-year-flight between two divine-messenger encounters at the boundaries of the Promised Land. The inclusio is editorially deliberate.

**The verb *paga*.** The chapter's v 2 verb *va-yifge'u* (qal of *paga* — *meet, encounter, fall upon*) shares the lexeme with Gen 28:11's *va-yifga ba-maqom* (*he encountered the place* — the Bethel ladder-vision opener). The *paga*-verb's range — accidental encounter / intentional meeting / falling-upon — is treated in the [paga-ba-maqom-cultic-encounter](#paga-ba-maqom-cultic-encounter) central-glossary entry. The Machanayim-encounter's *va-yifge'u* (3mp — the messengers are the active subject; they meet Ya'aqov) inverts Gen 28:11's *va-yifga* (3ms — Ya'aqov encounters the place). The grammatical-subject inversion is editorially significant: at Bethel, Ya'aqov stumbles upon the sacred site; at Machanayim, the divine-messengers meet him.

**The translation choice.** The WoH renders *Machanayim* (transliterated, matching the WoH place-name convention; the apostrophe of *Mahanaim* in some transliterations is absent here per WoH practice). The dual-form etymology is preserved as in-text Hebrew (the verse retains *machaneh Elohim zeh*) and is surfaced in commentary. The alternative *Two Camps* (semantic translation) is documented as a defensible variant and is not adopted to preserve the place-name's proper-noun-status.

**Modern scholarly literature.** Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 223-224; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 506-507; Wenham *WBC Genesis 16-50* 1994 pp. 286-287; Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 pp. 320-322; Speiser *AB Genesis* 1964 pp. 254-255; Alter *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 180; von Rad *Genesis* OTL 1972 p. 315; for the cross-corpus geography: **Z. Kallai** *Historical Geography of the Bible* 1986; **Aharoni** *The Land of the Bible* 1979; NEAEHL on the Tell el-Hajjaj / Tell edh-Dhahab site-identifications proposed for the historical Machanayim. The claim_type is *direct* because (a) the dual-form *machanayim* is grammatically explicit; (b) the in-text etymology *machaneh Elohim zeh* is grammatically explicit; (c) the cross-corpus distribution is verifiable by lexical search; (d) the two-reading ambiguity is documented in the standard commentaries and presented as parallel positions; (e) the Bethel-Machanayim inclusio is HB-internal-explicit through the plural-*mal'akhei Elohim* verbal echo.

terms.translit: akhapprah panav ba-minchah
terms.partOfSpeech: verb (piel cohortative 1cs) + noun-with-3ms-suffix + preposition-with-definite-article + noun
terms.literal: I-will-cover / I-will-atone-for his-face with-the-gift
terms.standardEnglish: I will appease him with the present (ASV/KJV); I may appease him with the present (NRSV); I will propitiate him with the gift (NJPS)
terms.wohChoice: I will appease his face with the present (preserving the *panim*-repetition without preserving *kipper*-literalness)
terms.rationale:
**Gen 32:21 (MT) loads two cultic-vocabulary lexemes onto Ya'aqov's inter-political tribute-strategy: the *piel kipper* (the canonical Levitical-atonement verb) and the four-fold *panim* (face) repetition. The verse's combination of these elements is editorially deliberate and is the chapter's most-articulated cultic-language-import.**

**The verse's structure.** Ya'aqov's instruction to his servants ends at v 21 with his interior-monologue rationale: *ki-amar akhapprah panav ba-minchah ha-holekhet l-fanai v-acharei-khen er'eh panav ulai yissa panai* — *for he said, I will cover/appease his face with the present that goes before my face, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will lift up my face*. The verse contains **four occurrences** of *panim* (face) — *panav* (his face) × 2, *fanai* (my face — preposed *l-fanai* = before my face) × 1, *fanai* (my face, accusative) × 1. The four-fold repetition is editorially deliberate and structurally anticipates the *panim el panim* of v 31 — the verse 21 *panav / panai* cluster prepares the v 31 *Peni'el* / *panim el panim* climax.

**(a) The *piel kipper* verb.** The *piel* of *k-p-r* (כָּפַר) is the canonical Levitical-atonement verb, used 92 times in the HB with the technical-cultic sense of *make atonement for, cover sin/impurity, expiate*. The verb's principal cultic-deployments: **Lev 16** (the Yom Kippur ritual — Aaron *makes atonement* for himself, his household, the sanctuary, and the people through the dual-goat sacrifice and the scapegoat-Azazel ritual); **Lev 4-7** (the *chatat*-and-*asham* sin-offering and guilt-offering legislation); **Num 8** (the Levite-consecration *kipper*); **Num 31** (the post-Midian-war purification *kipper*). The lexeme's cultic-semantic core: the priestly action that *covers* or *removes* the impurity or sin standing between the worshiper and the deity.

The verb's **non-cultic / pre-cultic deployments** are far rarer. The Gen 32:21 occurrence is one of the most-cited non-cultic occurrences: Ya'aqov uses the cultic-verb in a manifestly inter-political context (a gift to Esav, not to a deity). The other principal non-cultic occurrences: **Prov 16:14** (*chamat-melekh mal'akhei mavet v-ish chakham yekhapprenah* — *the wrath of a king is messengers of death, but a wise man will appease it* — the same king-anger-appeasement register); **Isa 28:18** (*v-khupar britkhem et-mavet* — *and your covenant with death shall be annulled* — *kipper* in the sense of *void / nullify*); **Jer 18:23** (*v-al-tekhapper al-avonam* — *do not cover their iniquity* — Jeremiah's imprecatory prayer). The non-cultic deployments cluster around the **appeasement / placation / annulment** sense, distinct from the technical-cultic *make-atonement* sense.

**The Gen 32:21 reading-positions.**

*(i) The deliberate cultic-vocabulary import.* **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 225-226 reads the verse as deliberately importing cultic-vocabulary into the inter-political tribute-context: Ya'aqov treats Esav as a quasi-divine-addressee in the appeasement-context, and the narrator's use of *kipper* + *minchah* marks the structural-analogy. The reading is sharpened by the *kipper panav* construction — *covering the face* — which echoes the **propitiation-of-the-deity** semantic (cf. the *seek the face* / *hide the face* / *lift up the face* family of HB divine-encounter formulae). **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 510-511 reads similarly.

*(ii) The pre-cultic appeasement-semantic.* An alternative reading: the *kipper*-verb at Gen 32 preserves a **pre-cultic appeasement-semantic** that predates the Levitical-cultic deployment. The lexeme's root meaning is *cover* (cf. the Akkadian *kapāru* — *wipe clean, smear*; the Arabic *kafara* — *cover, conceal*); the **technical-cultic atonement-sense** developed from this root-meaning in the Levitical legislation, and the Gen 32 occurrence preserves the older non-technical sense. On this reading, the verb's appearance at Gen 32:21 is not a cultic-vocabulary-import but a witness to the lexeme's pre-cultic semantic-range. **Milgrom** *Leviticus 1-16* AB 1991 pp. 1079-1084 develops the *cover / wipe* root-semantic; **HALOT** s.v. *kafar* reviews the etymology.

The two readings are not mutually exclusive: the verb's pre-cultic appeasement-semantic is consistent with the lexeme's continuity across the HB, and the narrator's deployment at v 21 may simultaneously preserve the older sense and resonate with the later cultic-development.

**(b) The four-fold *panim* cluster.** The chapter's *panim* (face) lexeme recurs ten times across vv 18-31 — the chapter's densest *panim*-concentration. The principal occurrences:

- **v 18** *l-panav* (before his face — narrator)
- **v 21** *panav* (his face), *l-fanai* (before my face), *panav* (his face), *panai* (my face) — the four-fold cluster
- **v 22** *al-panav* (before his face — narrator)
- **v 31** *Peni'el* (face-of-El — toponym), *panim el panim* (face to face — formula)
- **v 32** *Penu'el* (face-of-El — variant toponym)

The ten-fold *panim*-cluster's editorial structure: Ya'aqov's strategy is to *send the gift before his face* (v 18, 21, 22) so that he can later *see Esav's face* (v 21) and *Esav will lift up his face* (v 21 — *yissa panai* — the *nasa panim* idiom for *grant favor*). The strategic-vocabulary then transitions to the night-encounter, where Ya'aqov sees a different face — Elohim's face — and the chapter climaxes with the *Peni'el* / *panim el panim* naming-formula. The chapter is structurally a *meeting-of-faces* narrative: gift-to-Esav's-face, wrestler-without-face, divine-face-of-El, sunrise-departure-from-the-face-of-El, sunset-Esav-encounter (in Gen 33). The *panim*-cluster is the chapter's structural-spine. **Alter** *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 pp. 180-181 and **Fokkelman** *Narrative Art in Genesis* 1975 (the foundational literary-critical treatment of the chapter) both develop the *panim*-cluster reading.

**The *nasa panim* idiom.** The v 21 closing clause *ulai yissa panai* (*perhaps he will lift up my face*) deploys the *nasa panim* (lift up the face) idiom — the standard HB construction for *show favor, accept the person, grant favorable judgment*. The idiom recurs at: **Gen 19:21** (the messenger to Lot: *hineh nasati panekha gam la-davar ha-zeh* — *behold, I have lifted up your face also concerning this matter* — the rescue-favor); **Gen 40:13, 19, 20** (the cupbearer / baker scene); **Lev 19:15** (the legal *lo tisa p'nei dal* — *do not lift up the face of the poor* — the legal-impartiality command); **Deut 10:17** (YHWH *asher lo yissa panim* — *who does not lift up the face* — the divine-impartiality affirmation); **Job 13:8, 32:21**; **Mal 1:8, 9**; **Mal 2:9**. The idiom names the *favor-granting* action through the metaphorical *raising-the-face* of the suppliant. Ya'aqov's *ulai yissa panai* is his hope that Esav will grant favor.

**The translation choice.** The WoH translation preserves the *panim*-repetition explicitly — *I will appease his face with the present that goes before my face, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will lift up my face* — against the ASV-baseline (*appease him*, *see his face*, *accept me*) which preserves only the middle *panim* and smooths the rest. The choice preserves the structural-anticipation of the v 31 *Peni'el* / *panim el panim* climax. The *kipper*-literalness is **not** preserved (the WoH renders *appease* rather than *cover* or *atone for*); the cultic-vocabulary resonance is documented in this glossary-entry's rationale rather than imposed on the translation-text. The compromise prioritizes the *panim*-cluster's structural-function over the *kipper*-lexeme's cultic-resonance.

**Modern scholarly literature.** Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 225-226; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 510-511; Wenham *WBC Genesis 16-50* 1994 pp. 290-292; Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 pp. 327-328; Speiser *AB Genesis* 1964 pp. 256-257; Alter *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 pp. 180-181; Fokkelman *Narrative Art in Genesis* 1975 pp. 197-200; von Rad *Genesis* OTL 1972 pp. 315-317; Milgrom *Leviticus 1-16* AB 1991 pp. 1079-1084 (on the *kipper*-etymology and the cover-wipe root-semantic); HALOT s.v. *kafar*; BDB s.v. *kafar* p. 497; TDOT VII:288-303; for the *nasa panim* idiom: Carpenter NIDOTTE III:160-163. The claim_type is *direct* because (a) the *piel kipper* verb is grammatically explicit; (b) the four-fold *panim* cluster is grammatically explicit; (c) the *kipper*'s cultic-vocabulary-import reading is mainstream modern critical (Sarna, Westermann); (d) the cross-corpus *kipper* distribution (cultic vs. non-cultic) is verifiable by lexical search; (e) the *panim*-cluster's structural-function across the chapter is documentary; (f) the *nasa panim* idiom's cross-corpus distribution is verifiable.

terms.partOfSpeech: toponym + verb (niphal impf 3ms vav-consec, *wrestled / struggled*) + proper noun
terms.literal: Yabboq (the river) / and-he-wrestled / Ya'aqov
terms.standardEnglish: Jabbok / wrestled / Jacob (ASV/KJV); Jabbok / wrestled / Jacob (NRSV); Jabbok / wrestled / Jacob (NJPS)
terms.wohChoice: Yabboq / wrestled / Ya'aqov (transliterated, paronomasia preserved through the WoH transliteration practice)
terms.rationale:
**Gen 32:23-25 (MT) deploys one of the HB's most-cited toponym-event word-plays: the three-fold paronomasia *Yabboq* (the river) / *va-ye'avek* (the wrestling-verb) / *Ya'aqov* (Jacob). The three terms share consonantal-clusters across the y-b-q / ʾ-b-q / y-ʿ-q-b root-families, producing a deliberate sound-resonance that binds the toponym, the action, and the patriarch's name into a single editorial-figure.**

**The three roots.**

*(i) Yabboq (יַבֹּק).* The toponym is the river-name of the trans-Jordanian wadi (modern Nahr ez-Zarqa, *Blue River*) that flows west into the Jordan c. 35 km north of the Dead Sea. The river forms the southern boundary of the Gad / Reuben territory in the Joshua-allocation (Josh 12:2; 13:9, 16) and is mentioned in the wider patriarchal-conquest narratives (Num 21:24 — the Amorite kingdom of Sichon north of the Yabboq; Deut 2:37; 3:16; Judg 11:13, 22). The toponym's etymology: BDB s.v. *Yabboq* p. 132 derives the name from the root *b-q-q* (*be empty, pour out*; cf. *baqaq* — *empty out*; *boqeq* — *one who empties*), with the *Yabboq* meaning *the pouring-out / the emptying* — a reference to the river's seasonal flood-pattern. The etymology is consistent with the river's hydrology but is post-facto in the chapter's narrative-frame.

*(ii) Va-ye'avek (וַיֵּאָבֵק).* The verb at v 25 is the **niphal** of the root *ʾ-b-q* (אָבַק) — *wrestle, struggle, grapple*. The root is rare in BH: the verb appears only twice in the HB (Gen 32:25 and 32:26), both within this chapter — the verbal hapax is confined to the wrestling-scene. The related noun *avaq* (אָבָק — *dust*) is more widely attested and derives from the same root (the *wrestling-dust* / the *kicked-up earth of a struggle*); the noun appears at Exod 9:9 (the dust of the boils-plague); Deut 28:24 (the dust of judgment); Isa 5:24, 29:5; Nah 1:3; Ezek 26:10. The verb-noun root-relationship is editorially significant: wrestling produces dust, and the dust-noun is the more-attested form, with the verb here preserved as a chapter-specific niphal-deployment.

*(iii) Ya'aqov (יַעֲקֹב).* The patriarch's name's standard etymology is the root *ʿ-q-b* (עָקַב) — *follow at the heel, supplant, deceive* — explicitly given at Gen 25:26 (the birth-narrative: *v-yado ochezet b-aqev Esav va-yiqra shmo Ya'aqov* — *and his hand was grasping the heel of Esav, and he called his name Ya'aqov*) and reactivated at Gen 27:36 (Esav's complaint after the stolen blessing: *ha-khi qara shmo Ya'aqov va-yaq'veni zeh fa'amayim* — *is it because his name is Ya'aqov that he has supplanted me these two times?*). The name's pejorative-resonance — *heel-grabber / supplanter / deceiver* — is editorially-developed across the Ya'aqov-cycle. The chapter's renaming to *Yisra'el* at v 29 is precisely the resolution of the *Ya'aqov* / supplanter problem.

**The paronomasia's editorial function.** The three roots share consonantal-clusters: *Yabboq* (y-b-q), *va-ye'avek* (ʾ-b-q in niphal), *Ya'aqov* (y-ʿ-q-b). The three forms share two consonants (b + q) consistently and overlap on a third (the *y* of Yabboq and Ya'aqov; the laryngeal of va-ye'avek and Ya'aqov). The paronomasia is **maximal** in a Hebrew sound-system that treats consonantal-resonance as the primary phonetic-organization. The reading: the chapter binds the toponym (*Yabboq*), the action (*va-ye'avek*), and the patriarch (*Ya'aqov*) into a single sound-cluster that the Hebrew reader cannot miss.

**The function.** Modern critical scholarship reads the paronomasia as marking the chapter's **central-transformation**: at the *Yabboq* ford, Ya'aqov *wrestles* and is renamed, and the sound-cluster *Yabboq / va-ye'avek / Ya'aqov* is itself transformed by the chapter's resolution into the new name *Yisra'el*. The sound-cluster names the chapter's old-identity (the *Ya'aqov* / heel-grabber bound to the *Yabboq* / pouring-out place through the *va-ye'avek* / struggle); the renaming to *Yisra'el* breaks the cluster.

**Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 226 reads the paronomasia as one of the chapter's most-deliberate features; **Alter** *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 181 develops the sound-cluster reading extensively (his commentary on the chapter is one of the strongest English-language treatments of the paronomasia); **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 514-515 notes the word-play; **Hamilton** *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 pp. 328-329 surfaces the cluster; **Fokkelman** *Narrative Art in Genesis* 1975 pp. 197-222 (the foundational literary-critical chapter-treatment) develops the paronomasia in extended close-reading. **Speiser** *AB Genesis* 1964 p. 255 reads the *Yabboq* etymology more conservatively.

**The translation choice.** The WoH preserves the paronomasia through the WoH transliteration practice: *Yabboq* (with the dagesh-preserved geminate), *wrestled* (the standard English equivalent for *va-ye'avek*), *Ya'aqov* (per the WoH proper-name convention). The English-reader does not see the full sound-cluster (the *Jabbok* / *Jacob* of standard English-translation collapses the y-b-q / y-ʿ-q-b distinction more than the Hebrew does), but the transliteration *Yabboq* / *Ya'aqov* surfaces the y-q resonance. The paronomasia is documented in this glossary-entry and in the chapter commentary; a serious source-language reader will recover the full cluster from the transliterated forms.

**Modern scholarly literature.** Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 226; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 514-515; Wenham *WBC Genesis 16-50* 1994 pp. 293-294; Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 pp. 328-329; Speiser *AB Genesis* 1964 pp. 255-256; Alter *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 181; Fokkelman *Narrative Art in Genesis* 1975 pp. 197-222 (the foundational literary-critical chapter-treatment); von Rad *Genesis* OTL 1972 pp. 317-319; for the *avaq* root: HALOT s.v. *avaq*; BDB s.v. *avaq* p. 7; for the *Yabboq* river-geography: Aharoni *The Land of the Bible* 1979; Z. Kallai *Historical Geography of the Bible* 1986. The claim_type is *direct* because (a) the three roots and their consonantal-clusters are grammatically explicit; (b) the chapter's deliberate-clustering of the three forms across vv 23-25 is documentary; (c) the wider literary-critical reading of the paronomasia as the chapter's structural-spine is mainstream modern critical (Sarna, Alter, Fokkelman); (d) the *avaq*-verb's chapter-specific hapax-status is verifiable by lexical search.

terms.partOfSpeech: verb (niphal impf 3ms vav-consec) + noun (man, person) + preposition-with-3ms-suffix
terms.literal: and-he-wrestled a-man with-him
terms.standardEnglish: and there wrestled a man with him (ASV/KJV); a man wrestled with him (NRSV); a man wrestled with him (NJPS)
terms.wohChoice: and there wrestled a man with him (ASV-baseline, lens-quiet; the chapter's silence on the *ish*'s identity preserved; the five interpretive traditions documented in this entry)
terms.rationale:
**LOAD-BEARING — the chapter's foundational interpretive crux. Gen 32:25 (MT) records the night-wrestling-encounter with these words: *va-yivater Ya'aqov l-vado va-ye'avek ish imo ad alot ha-shachar* — *and Ya'aqov was left alone, and an ish wrestled with him until the breaking of the dawn*. The wrestler is designated only as *ish* — a man, an unnamed human-form figure. The narrator never resolves the *ish*'s identity. The chapter's silence on this point has generated five major interpretive traditions, all of which the WoH translation preserves in parallel without project-preemption.**

**The textual datum.** Across vv 25-31, the wrestler is designated:
- **v 25**: *ish* (a man — without article)
- **v 26**: subject-pronoun only (*va-yar ki lo yakhol lo* — *and he saw that he prevailed not against him*)
- **v 27**: subject-pronoun only (*va-yomer shalcheni* — *and he said, let me go*)
- **v 28**: subject-pronoun only (the name-asking exchange)
- **v 29**: the wrestler's own self-witness via the renaming-formula (*ki-sarita im-Elohim v-im-anashim* — *for you have striven with Elohim and with men*, see the companion `yisrael-name-aetiology-sarah-im-elohim` entry)
- **v 30**: subject-pronoun only (the name-refusal — *lamah zeh tish'al li-shmi*)
- **v 31**: Ya'aqov's interpretive-naming of the place (*Peni'el ki-ra'iti Elohim panim el panim*) — Ya'aqov reads the encounter as a face-of-Elohim encounter

The textual structure: the narrator names the wrestler only as *ish*; the wrestler self-identifies (indirectly, through v 29's renaming-formula) as one with whom Ya'aqov has *striven with Elohim and with men* (an ambiguous formula — see the companion entry); and Ya'aqov interprets the encounter (at v 31) as a face-of-Elohim encounter. The narrator never directly resolves the identity-question.

**The five interpretive traditions.**

**Reading 1: The *ish* as *malʾakh* / divine messenger.** The reading is supported by the **Hosea 12:4-5 reception**: the prophet reads the chapter's wrestling-figure as a *mal'akh*. *Vayasar el-mal'akh va-yukhal bakhah v-yitchanen lo* — *and he strove with a messenger and prevailed; he wept and made supplication to him* (Hos 12:4-5, MT 12:5-6). The Hosea reading is the earliest HB-internal interpretation of the *ish*'s identity, and identifies the wrestler as a *mal'akh*. Supported in modern critical scholarship by **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 226 (as a defensible reading, alongside the YHWH-himself reading); **Hamori** *When Gods Were Men* 2008 (treats the *ish* as the embodied-divine-messenger type alongside Gen 18). The reading is widely held in Jewish and Christian tradition.

**Reading 2: The *ish* as YHWH himself / pre-incarnate Christophany.** The reading reads Hosea 12:4-5 as a parallelistic-doublet: *va-yasar et-Elohim* (he strove with Elohim) // *va-yasar el-mal'akh* (he strove with a messenger). The doublet would identify Elohim and the *mal'akh* — making the wrestler YHWH-himself or a theophany-form of YHWH. The reading is classically the **patristic Christophany-reading**: read by **Justin Martyr** *Dialogue with Trypho* 58, 86, 125-126; **Irenaeus** *Adversus Haereses* IV.10.1; **Tertullian** *Adversus Praxean* 16; **Augustine** *Contra Faustum* 22:84; *De Trinitate* II.18, who reads the wrestler as the pre-incarnate Logos / Christ. The reading recurs in modern critical scholarship at **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 514-520 (treats the wrestler as a YHWH-theophany); **von Rad** *Genesis* OTL 1972 pp. 319-321 (a YHWH-encounter); **Brueggemann** *Genesis* Interpretation 1982 pp. 269-270. The reading sits comfortably with Ya'aqov's v 31 interpretation (*ra'iti Elohim panim el panim*).

**Reading 3: The *ish* as Esav's guardian-angel / Samael / Sariel.** The reading is the dominant Jewish midrashic-tradition reading: the wrestler is the cosmic-angelic-representative of Esav, identified variously as **Samael** (the standard rabbinic-tradition name for Esav's guardian-angel, drawing on the wider angelological tradition of nation-guardian-angels), **Sariel**, or simply *saro shel Esav* (the prince of Esav). The reading is developed extensively in:
- **Genesis Rabbah 77:3, 78:3** (the Esav-guardian-angel identification)
- **Targum Pseudo-Jonathan** at Gen 32:25 (identifies the *ish* as *Saraf-el / Sariel* — a chief-angel-figure of Esav)
- **Rashi at Gen 32:25** (citing Genesis Rabbah, the *saro shel Esav*)
- **Targum Onkelos** at Gen 32:25 (renders *ish* as *gavra* — *man / hero* — preserving the surface-text without committing)
- **Zohar** I:170a-171a, 173a (develops the angelological-cosmic-conflict reading)

The reading frames the wrestling as a cosmic-prefiguration of the Esav-encounter at Gen 33: by prevailing over Esav's guardian-angel, Ya'aqov ensures victory over Esav himself. The reading explains the chapter's narrative-juxtaposition (the angel-wrestling immediately precedes the Esav-encounter).

**Reading 4: The *ish* as river-numen / night-spirit / chthonic-being.** The classical history-of-religions reading: the wrestler is a *Flussdämon* (river-demon) or chthonic night-spirit, a vestige of pre-Israelite folkloric-tradition imported into the patriarchal narrative. The reading is developed extensively in:
- **Hermann Gunkel** *Genesis* (1901; 3rd ed. 1910; ET 1997 pp. 348-352) — the foundational presentation; reads the wrestler as a river-numen of the Yabboq, constrained by daylight, vanquished or appeased by the patriarch's persistent grip
- **J. G. Frazer** *Folklore in the Old Testament* III (1918) pp. 410-456 — develops Gunkel's reading with extensive cross-cultural comparative material on river-spirits and night-beings
- **Hugo Gressmann** *Mose und seine Zeit* (1913) — the wider history-of-religions framework
- **Hermann Schmidt** *Mythos und Märchen in Altisrael* (1923)
- **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 514-516 (acknowledges the tradition; partial acceptance; prefers the YHWH-theophany reading)

The reading's strengths: explains the dawn-constraint (the *ish* must leave at dawn — characteristic of chthonic / night-beings); explains the wrestling-mode (chthonic-beings are conventionally wrestled-with rather than encountered-by-revelation); explains the name-refusal (magical-name protection); explains the wound (the chthonic-being's parting-mark on the human). The reading reframes the chapter as a theologized-folkloric narrative: the older river-numen tradition has been preserved but reinterpreted as a YHWH-encounter.

**Reading 5: The *ish* as Ya'aqov's internal-other / psychological-symbolic.** The modern literary-critical and depth-psychological reading: the wrestler is Ya'aqov's projected internal-other — his unresolved-Esav, his unintegrated-shadow, his repressed-deception, his conscience-figure. The reading is developed at:
- **Carl Jung** *Symbols of Transformation* and the wider analytical-psychology Genesis-readings (the *night-sea-journey* archetype)
- **J. P. Fokkelman** *Narrative Art in Genesis: Specimens of Stylistic and Structural Analysis* (1975) pp. 197-222 — the foundational literary-critical chapter-treatment; reads the wrestler as Ya'aqov's psychological-projection and the wrestling as the patriarch's internal-confrontation with his deceptive-past
- **Walter Wink** *Engaging the Powers* (1992)
- **Roger L. Cox** *The Psychology of Genesis* (1996)
- **Kathryn Schifferdecker** numerous treatments

The reading frames the wrestling as Ya'aqov's interior-event: alone at the Yabboq, on the eve of meeting Esav, Ya'aqov wrestles with himself / his deception / his anxieties. The chapter's psychological-realism and the wrestler's-identity-mystery are read as deliberate literary devices for staging Ya'aqov's interior-transformation.

**The chapter's silence as editorial-strategy.** The five readings are not strictly mutually exclusive — the chapter's interpretive-power derives precisely from its silence. Different readings illuminate different aspects of the narrative; the chapter sustains all five without resolving in favor of any one. The narrator's deliberate-non-resolution is the editorial datum. **Fokkelman** *Narrative Art* 1975 pp. 197-222 reads this most explicitly: the chapter's *ish* is **deliberately under-determined** as a literary strategy that invites multiple readings.

**The Wheel of Heaven lens-distinctive position.** The WoH lens reads the *ish* as a **physical divine-being / spacecraft-occupant** — a Raelian / ancient-astronaut-tradition reading consistent with the project's wider hypothesis that the patriarchal-Elohim are an advanced human civilization. The lens-reading is a sixth reading-position. **The lens-reading is reserved for the wiki and is not preempted by this glossary entry.** The translation preserves the textual silence — *ish* rendered as *a man* (ASV-baseline) — and documents the five mainstream interpretive traditions without project-preemption. The lens-distinctive synthesis is recorded in the project's wiki on *Penuel* and the *ish*, not in the translation's apparatus.

**The discipline-rationale.** The chapter's editorial-silence is itself the strongest argument for translation-discipline at this verse. A translation that resolved the *ish*'s identity in favor of the lens-reading would over-step the source: the source does not say. A translation that resolved in favor of any of the five mainstream readings would equally over-step. The discipline is to preserve the silence, document the readings, and reserve the lens-synthesis for the wiki where it can be argued on its own terms.

**The translation choice.** The WoH renders *and there wrestled a man with him* (ASV-baseline; the chapter's silence preserved). The five mainstream interpretive traditions are documented in this glossary-entry. The lens-distinctive synthesis is reserved for the wiki.

**Modern scholarly literature.** Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 226-228; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 514-524; Wenham *WBC Genesis 16-50* 1994 pp. 292-298; Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 pp. 326-336; Speiser *AB Genesis* 1964 pp. 254-258; Alter *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 pp. 181-183; von Rad *Genesis* OTL 1972 pp. 319-322; Brueggemann *Genesis* Interpretation 1982 pp. 268-273; Fokkelman *Narrative Art in Genesis* 1975 pp. 197-222; Gunkel *Genesis* 1901/1910 pp. 348-352; Frazer *Folklore in the Old Testament* III 1918 pp. 410-456; Hamori *When Gods Were Men* 2008; Smith *The Early History of God* 1990/2002. Rabbinic-tradition: Genesis Rabbah 77:3, 78:3; b. Chullin 91a-92a; Targum Pseudo-Jonathan at Gen 32:25; Rashi ad loc.; Zohar I:170a-171a. Patristic-tradition: Justin Martyr *Dialogue with Trypho* 58, 86, 125-126; Irenaeus *Adversus Haereses* IV.10.1; Tertullian *Adversus Praxean* 16; Augustine *Contra Faustum* 22:84, *De Trinitate* II.18. The claim_type is *direct* because (a) the *ish* designation is grammatically explicit; (b) the chapter's silence on the *ish*'s identity is documentary; (c) the five interpretive traditions are well-attested in the cited literature (Hosea 12 + modern critical for Reading 1; patristic + Westermann for Reading 2; rabbinic for Reading 3; Gunkel-Frazer-history-of-religions for Reading 4; literary-critical / depth-psychological for Reading 5); (d) the editorial-silence-as-strategy reading is mainstream literary-critical consensus (Fokkelman, Alter); (e) the lens-distinctive sixth reading is explicitly reserved for the wiki and not preempted in the translation or this entry.

terms.strongs: H5060 (naga) + H3709 (kaf) + H3409 (yarekh) + H3363 (yaqa, niphal — to be dislocated/strained)
terms.partOfSpeech: verb (qal impf 3ms, vav-consec) + preposition + construct-noun + noun-with-3ms-suffix + verb (qal impf 3fs, vav-consec) + construct-noun + noun + proper noun
terms.literal: and-he-touched at-the-hollow of-his-thigh, and-was-dislocated the-hollow of-thigh of-Ya'aqov
terms.standardEnglish: and he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was strained (ASV/KJV); he struck him on the hip socket, and Jacob's hip was put out of joint (NRSV); he struck the socket of his hip, so that the socket of his hip was wrenched (NJPS)
terms.wohChoice: and he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Ya'aqov's thigh was strained (ASV-baseline; the anatomical specifics and the euphemism-question surfaced in commentary)
terms.rationale:
**Gen 32:26 records the wrestling's decisive moment: *va-yar ki lo yakhol lo va-yiga b-khaf-yerekho va-teqa kaf-yerekh Ya'aqov b-he'avqo imo* — *and when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Ya'aqov's thigh was strained as he wrestled with him*. The verse's anatomical specificity is unusual in HB narrative and has generated extensive editorial discussion on (a) what part of the body is meant; (b) the euphemistic-register of *naga* (touch); (c) the precise injury inflicted.**

**The lexemes.**

*(i) Kaf ha-yarekh.* The construct *kaf ha-yarekh* (the hollow / palm / cup of the thigh) combines *kaf* (כַּף — the cup-shaped curved-surface of palm-of-hand, sole-of-foot, or socket-of-joint) with *yarekh* (יָרֵךְ — thigh, upper-leg, hip-region, by extension reproductive-organs / genital-area in some HB contexts). The construct names a **cup-shaped anatomical region of the upper-thigh** — most naturally the **hip-socket** (the *acetabulum* of the pelvis), though older renderings *hollow of the thigh* and *palm of the thigh* preserve the literal *kaf*-lexeme. The construct recurs only here in the HB; the related construct *yad on kaf-yad* recurs more widely (the *kaf* / *yad* / palm-and-hand of the hand-region).

The broader *yarekh* lexeme has two principal HB ranges: (a) **upper-thigh / hip-region** (Gen 24:2, 9; 47:29 — the *yad-tachat-yarekh* oath-gesture; Num 5:21-27 — the *adultery-suspicion ordeal's *yarekh* swelling; Judg 3:21 — Ehud's left-thigh sword-concealment; etc.); (b) **reproductive-organs / loins** as a euphemistic-reference to genitals or fertility (Gen 46:26 — *kol-nefesh ha-ba'ah l-Ya'aqov Mitsraymah yotzei yerekho* — *all the souls who came with Ya'aqov to Mitsrayim, who came forth from his thigh* — the descent-from-the-loins idiom; Exod 1:5; Judg 8:30 — *Gid'on's seventy sons yotzei yerekho* — *who came forth from his loins*). The *yarekh* lexeme's range from upper-thigh to genital-reproductive-region produces the chapter's interpretive question on whether *kaf-yerekh* is anatomical or euphemistic.

*(ii) Naga (touch).* The verb *naga* (qal of *n-g-ʿ* — *touch, reach, strike, smite*) has a range from neutral-contact (Gen 3:3 — touching the tree of knowledge) to violent-striking (1 Sam 6:9 — the disease that *touches* the Philistines) to **euphemistic-sexual-contact** (Gen 20:6 — Avimelekh did not *touch* Sarah; Gen 26:11 — Avimelekh's decree that whoever *touches* Rivkah or Yitzchaq dies; Prov 6:29 — the man who *touches* his neighbor's wife). The verb's deployment at Gen 32:26 in the *yarekh*-region produces the rabbinic-tradition reading.

*(iii) Va-teqa.* The verb *va-teqa* (niphal of *y-q-ʿ* or *t-q-ʿ* — the lexicographies disagree on the root; HALOT s.v. *yqʿ* II) means *to be dislocated, displaced, wrenched, put out of joint*. The verb is rare in BH (the qal *t-q-ʿ* — *blow [a horn], drive [a tent peg], strike [a hand-clasp]* — is widely attested; the niphal *yqʿ / tqʿ* in the dislocation-sense is restricted). The related noun *teqa* (*dislocation* / *wedge*) is post-biblical. The verb names the wrestling-wound's mechanism: a forced-displacement of the hip-socket joint.

**The anatomical / euphemistic reading-question.**

*(i) The anatomical reading.* The hip-socket dislocation — the *acetabulum* dislocated from the *femoral head* — is consistent with the wrestling-mechanism and with the limping-aftermath at v 32 (*v-hu tzole'a al-yerekho* — *he was limping upon his thigh*). The reading is supported by **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 227; **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 517-518; **Speiser** *AB Genesis* 1964 p. 255; **NJPS** renders *struck the socket of his hip*; **NRSV** *struck him on the hip socket*. The reading is the modern critical default.

*(ii) The genital / euphemistic reading.* The rabbinic-tradition reading at **Genesis Rabbah 77:3** reads *kaf-yerekh* as a euphemism for the genital-region, making the wound a wounding-of-the-male-fertility / sexual-organ-injury. The reading draws on the *yarekh*-as-loins-euphemism elsewhere in the HB (Gen 46:26; Judg 8:30) and on the *naga*-as-sexual-contact register (Gen 20:6; 26:11; Prov 6:29). The reading is preserved in some translations (older Latin Vulgate readings, some medieval Jewish commentaries) and rejected in others. **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 519-520 reviews the position and rejects it; **Hamilton** *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 pp. 329-330 surfaces it; **Sarna** p. 227 notes it. The modern critical scholarship is divided but generally prefers the anatomical reading.

*(iii) The sciatic-nerve / sinew reading.* A third reading: the touched-region is the **sciatic-nerve / nervus ischiadicus**, with the wound being a nerve-damage that produces the limping-aftermath. The reading is implicit in the v 33 aetiology of the *gid ha-nasheh* (see the companion `gid-ha-nasheh-sciatic-nerve-dietary-rule` entry) and is the rabbinic-halakhic identification of the *gid ha-nasheh* (m. Chullin 7; b. Chullin 91a). The reading is consistent with the limping-aftermath but reads *kaf-yerekh* less literally than the hip-socket reading.

**The wider ANE combat-injury tradition.** The hip-injury / thigh-wound motif in combat-stories is widely attested across ANE literature. Examples include the Mesopotamian Gilgamesh-Humbaba and Gilgamesh-Enkidu confrontations (no exact thigh-injury parallel but extensive close-combat motifs); the Hittite Tashmishu / Kumarbi mythological cycle; the Ugaritic Baal-Mot conflict. The motif's significance: combat-injuries that mark the victor or the survivor with a permanent-physical-trace are a wide ANE narrative-trope, and the chapter's wrestling-wound + limping-aftermath sits comfortably within this tradition. **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 517-518 and **Cross** *Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic* 1973 ch. 1-3 review the comparative-material.

**The aetiological-function.** The wound's editorial-function within the chapter is to establish the **physical-aftermath** of the encounter, which (a) confirms the encounter's reality (Ya'aqov does not merely dream or vision — he is physically marked); (b) supplies the in-text aetiology of the v 33 dietary-rule (the *gid ha-nasheh* prohibition); (c) marks Ya'aqov's transformation as bodily-inscribed, not merely name-inscribed. The wound is the physical-mark of the name-change.

**Translation choice.** The WoH renders *and he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Ya'aqov's thigh was strained* (ASV-baseline). The choice preserves the construct *kaf-yerekh* literally (*hollow of the thigh*) without resolving the anatomical / euphemistic question, and preserves *va-teqa* as *was strained* (the ASV reading, slightly weaker than *dislocated* but more cautious about the precise injury-mechanism). The euphemism-question is documented in commentary; the anatomical-reading-as-default is documented in this glossary-entry. More-modern renderings (*hip socket* / *put out of joint*) are noted as defensible variants.

**Modern scholarly literature.** Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 227; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 517-520; Wenham *WBC Genesis 16-50* 1994 pp. 294-295; Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 pp. 329-330; Speiser *AB Genesis* 1964 p. 255; Alter *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 182; for the *yarekh* lexeme: HALOT s.v. *yarekh*; BDB s.v. *yarekh* p. 437; for the *naga* euphemism: HALOT s.v. *nagaʿ*; TDOT IX:203-209; for the rabbinic-tradition reading: Genesis Rabbah 77:3; b. Chullin 91a; Rashi at Gen 32:26. The claim_type is *direct* because (a) the lexemes *kaf-yerekh*, *naga*, *va-teqa* are grammatically explicit; (b) the lexical ranges of *yarekh* (upper-thigh / loins-euphemism) and *naga* (touch / sexual-euphemism) are documentary; (c) the anatomical / euphemistic reading-question is documented in the standard commentaries; (d) the in-text limping-aftermath at v 32 confirms a physical-injury; (e) the v 33 dietary-rule aetiology HB-internal-explicitly grounds the wound's significance.
