terms.partOfSpeech: noun-phrase office-title: the kinship-noun av ('father') deployed as the Egyptian-court office-title for senior advisor / vizier
terms.literal: av le-Par'oh — a father to Pharaoh; the Egyptian-court office-title 'father' for the role of senior advisor / vizier / chief minister
terms.standardEnglish: a father to Pharaoh (ASV/KJV/NRSV); a father to Pharaoh (NJPS, identical); father to Pharaoh (modern, identical)
terms.wohChoice: a father to Pharaoh (ASV-baseline preserved; the Egyptian-court 'father' office-title and the cross-corpus 'father' / patriarchal-honorific-office-title parallels documented in commentary)
terms.rationale: **Gen 45:8 stages Yosef's three-fold office-title declaration: *va-yesimeni le-av le-Par'oh u-le-adon le-khol beito u-moshel be-khol eretz Mitzrayim* — 'and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Mitsrayim'. The first of the three titles — *av le-Par'oh* ('a father to Pharaoh') — is the chapter's principal interpretive crux. The construction is metaphorical, not familial (Yosef is obviously not Pharaoh's biological father); the metaphorical 'father' designates the office of senior advisor / vizier / chief minister. The Egyptian-court 'father' office-title is widely-discussed in the Egyptological literature and provides the historical-cultural anchor for the metaphorical-construction.** // **The construction.** The Hebrew *av* (אָב) is the standard kinship-noun 'father', with a substantial metaphorical / honorific / titular extension across the HB. The metaphorical-'father' is deployed for the patriarchal-honorific in multiple registers: (a) the founder-of-a-craft register (Gen 4:20-21, *avi yoshev ohel u-miqneh* + *avi kol tofes kinor ve-ugav* — Yaval and Yuval as the *fathers* of pastoralism and music); (b) the senior-advisor / royal-counselor register (Gen 45:8 here; 2 Chr 2:13 *Huram-Abi*; the cross-corpus material below); (c) the prophet / spiritual-mentor register (2 Kgs 2:12 *avi avi* — Elisha to Eliyahu; the prophetic-mentorship sense); (d) the protector / provider register (Job 29:16 *av anokhi la-evyonim* — Iyov as 'a father to the needy'; Isa 22:21 *u-le-av le-yoshev Yerushalayim u-le-veit Yehudah* — Eliyaqim as 'a father to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim'). The Gen 45:8 deployment is in the senior-advisor / royal-counselor register: Yosef is the *av*-to-Pharaoh in the sense of being the king's-chief-counselor. // **The Egyptian-court 'father' office-title.** The Egyptological literature attests the existence of senior-court office-titles using the kinship-metaphor 'father'. The principal candidates: (a) the *it-ntr* ('father of the god' / 'god's father') office, attested across multiple Egyptian periods as a senior religious-and-court office-title (used for the high-ranking priesthood and for senior royal counselors); (b) the Aramaic *abu-melekh* ('father of the king') designation, attested in some periods for chief vizier / chief advisor roles; (c) the broader 'father'-honorific in ancient-Near-Eastern court protocol, used to designate the king's senior-counselor or the regent / co-ruler role. The Egyptological scholarship: P. Vergote *Joseph en Égypte* OBL 3, 1959 pp. 113-128 (the canonical treatment); D. B. Redford *A Study of the Biblical Story of Joseph* VTSup 20, 1970 pp. 187-191; K. A. Kitchen *Reliability of the Old Testament* 2003 pp. 350-352. The named scholarship treats the *av le-Par'oh* title as historically-plausible Egyptian-court ethnography reflecting either the Hyksos-period administrative system or the later New Kingdom vizier-system. NO single Egyptian title is identified as the *exact* historical-original of the biblical *av le-Par'oh*; the scholarship documents the broader Egyptian-court 'father'-office-title pattern as the cultural-context. // **The cross-corpus parallels.** **2 Chr 2:13** — Huram of Tzor sends his master-craftsman Huram-Abi to Shelomoh: *ve-attah shalachti ish chakham yodea binah le-Huram avi* — 'I have sent a skillful man, endued with understanding, of Huram my father'. The construction *Huram avi* is the master-craftsman-as-father designation; the *avi* names the craftsman as a 'father' to the Tyrian court (in the senior-craftsman / royal-craftsman register). **Isa 22:21** — the deposition of Shevna and appointment of Elyaqim: *ve-hilbashtiv kuttontekha ve-avnetkha achazzqennu... ve-natati memshaltkha be-yado, ve-hayah le-av le-yoshev Yerushalayim u-le-veit Yehudah* — 'and I will clothe him with thy robe, and strengthen him with thy girdle... and I will commit thy government into his hand: and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, and to the house of Yehudah'. The Isaian deployment names the senior-royal-advisor / vizier role with the same metaphorical-'father'-construction; the Isaian Elyaqim-installation echoes the Gen 45:8 Yosef-installation lexically (the same *le-av le-* construction). **Job 29:16** — Iyov's self-description in the courtroom-scene: *av anokhi la-evyonim ve-riv lo-yadati echqerennu* ('I was a father to the needy: and the cause of him that I knew not I searched out') — the protector / provider sense. The cross-corpus deployments establish the metaphorical-'father' as a recognized HB honorific-office-title pattern. // **Overlay housing.** Chapter-specific Egyptian-court office-title deployment; the cross-corpus parallels (2 Chr 2:13, Isa 22:21, Job 29:16) are noted; the broader 'father' / patriarchal-honorific-office construction has cross-corpus reach. → **OVERLAY** with the cross-corpus parallels documented and noted as a possible promotion-seed when those texts are translated. // The claim_type is *inferred* because (a) the construction is metaphorical rather than literal (so the grammatical-fact and the office-title-identification require interpretation); (b) the precise Egyptian-court office-title underlying the *av le-Par'oh* is debated (no single Egyptian title is identified as the exact source; the broader Egyptian-court 'father'-office-title pattern is the scholarly-documented context); (c) the cross-corpus parallels are themselves interpretively-treated office-title deployments. The named-scholarship Egyptological literature (Vergote, Redford, Kitchen) and the cross-corpus literary parallels (2 Chr 2:13, Isa 22:21, Job 29:16) provide the documented basis. Named scholarship only; no project synthesis. // **Scholarly literature.** HALOT s.v. *av*; BDB pp. 1-3; TDOT I:1-19; NIDOTTE 1:219-223; Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 309; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* 1986 p. 144; Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 p. 576; Speiser *AB Genesis* 1964 p. 339; on the Egyptian-court 'father' office-title and the Vergote / Redford / Kitchen literature: P. Vergote *Joseph en Égypte* OBL 3, 1959 pp. 113-128; D. B. Redford *A Study of the Biblical Story of Joseph* VTSup 20, 1970 pp. 187-191; K. A. terms.literal: ve-khilkalti — and I will sustain / nourish / provide for [thee]; the Pilpel of kul in the active-causative sustenance-providing register
terms.standardEnglish: I will nourish (ASV/KJV); I will provide (NJPS); I will sustain (modern)
terms.wohChoice: I will nourish (ASV-baseline preserved; the Yosef-cycle's three-fold sustenance-promise arc Gen 45:11 + 47:12 + 50:21 documented; cross-corpus reach noted)
terms.rationale: **Gen 45:11 stages Yosef's sustenance-promise to Ya'aqov: *ve-khilkalti otkha sham ki-od chamesh shanim ra'av pen-tivvaresh attah u-veitkha ve-khol asher-lakh* — 'and there will I nourish thee; for there are yet five years of famine; lest thou come to poverty, thou, and thy household, and all that thou hast'. The verb is the Pilpel of *kul* ('contain, sustain'), the standard HB sustenance / provision lexeme. The Pilpel-stem of geminate-root verbs is the doubled-active register: the verb's force is the active-causative 'to provide-the-means-of-living'. The lexeme deploys across the Yosef-cycle in a structural three-fold sustenance-promise arc: Gen 45:11 (here, Yosef's promise to Ya'aqov); Gen 47:12 (the fulfilment, *va-yekhalkel Yosef et-aviv ve-et-echav ve-et kol-beit aviv lechem le-fi ha-taf*); Gen 50:21 (the post-Ya'aqov-death repetition to the brothers, *ve-attah al-tira'u anokhi achalkel etkhem ve-et-tappkhem*). The cycle's sustenance-promise arc anchors Yosef's pastoral-protective relation to the family across the descent + sojourn + post-death scenes.** // **The lexeme.** *Kul* (כול) in the Qal carries the basic sense 'to contain, hold, comprehend'; the Pilpel intensifies to 'sustain, provide-the-means-of-life, support'. The Pilpel-stem's semantic-core is the *active-causative* of the basic-sense: containment → sustenance, holding → providing-for. The lexeme is one of the corpus's principal sustenance-and-provision verbs, distinct from the broader *parnes* / *tzud* / *kun* sustenance-lexicon by its specific containment-and-support register. // **The cross-corpus distribution.** The Pilpel of *kul* is extensively distributed: **2 Sam 19:33-34 [MT 19:33-34]** (Barzilai sustaining David: *u-Varzillai... hu khilkel et-ha-melekh be-shivato be-Machanayim ki ish gadol hu me'od*); **1 Kgs 4:7** (the twelve officers sustaining Shelomoh's household: *ve-khilkelu et-ha-melekh ve-et-beito*); **1 Kgs 17:4 + 9** (Eliyahu sustained by the ravens at the Kerit + the Tzarphat widow: *et-ha-orevim tzivviti le-khalkelkha sham*; *hinneh tzivviti sham ishah almanah le-khalkelekha*); **1 Kgs 18:4 + 13** (Obadyah sustaining the prophets in the cave: *va-yekhalkelem*); **1 Kgs 20:27**; **Neh 9:21**; **Ps 55:23** (*ve-hu yekhalkelekha*, the divine-sustenance promise); the post-exilic deployments. terms.translit: fi ha-medabber aleikhem (Gen 45:12 ki-fi ha-medabber aleikhem, 'that it is my mouth that speaketh unto you')
terms.partOfSpeech: noun-phrase + participle construction; the marked emphasis on Yosef's MOUTH speaking directly, contrasted with the Gen 42:23 melitz mediation
terms.literal: fi ha-medabber aleikhem — my mouth, the one that is speaking unto you; the marked emphasis on direct unmediated speech in Hebrew
terms.standardEnglish: my mouth that speaketh unto you (ASV/KJV); it is my mouth that is speaking to you (NJPS); it is my own mouth speaking to you (Alter)
terms.wohChoice: my mouth that speaketh unto you (ASV-baseline preserved; the speech-mediation structural-reversal of the Gen 42:23 melitz documented in commentary; sibling-link to `melitz-interpreter-rare-sense-gen42`)
terms.rationale: **Gen 45:12 stages Yosef's marked emphasis on his MOUTH speaking directly to the brothers: *ve-hinneh eineikhem ro'ot ve-einei achi Vinyamin ki-fi ha-medabber aleikhem* — 'and, behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Binyamin, that it is my mouth that speaketh unto you'. The construction's force is the EXPLICIT LITERARY REVERSAL of Gen 42:23's *ki ha-melitz beinotam* ('for there was an interpreter between them'), governed by the SIBLING overlay [`melitz-interpreter-rare-sense-gen42`](#melitz-interpreter-rare-sense-gen42). At Gen 42:23 the cycle deploys the institutional court-interpreter as the speech-mediator (the brothers see Egyptian-court-protocol-mediation, not the *shallit*-who-understands-Hebrew-directly); at Gen 45:12 the interpreter-mediation is dispensed-with, and the marked emphasis falls on Yosef's *peh* (mouth) speaking directly in Hebrew. The mediated-speech / direct-speech pair is the cycle's principal speech-mediation literary structure.** // **The construction.** The Hebrew *fi ha-medabber aleikhem* is a marked nominal-construction: the noun *peh* ('mouth') with first-person-singular pronominal suffix (*fi*, 'my mouth') in subject-position; the definite-article + Piel-participle of *davar* (*ha-medabber*, 'the one speaking'); the *aleikhem* preposition ('unto you'). The construction emphasizes the SOURCE of the speech (it is Yosef's mouth, not the interpreter's mouth, that is the locus of the speaking-event) and the DIRECTNESS of the speech (the addressees can see directly that Yosef is the speaker). The double-witness structure (*einei... ve-einei achi Vinyamin*, 'your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Binyamin') reinforces the directness: the brothers can SEE (visually verify) that the speech is unmediated. The construction's literary force is the dropping-of-the-mediation: the mask of court-protocol comes off, and the brother-relation is verbally explicit. // **The cycle's mediated-speech / direct-speech reversal.** The cycle's speech-mediation structure is one of its principal literary-architectures. At the brothers' first-arrival (Gen 42), Yosef-the-shallit maintains the Egyptian-court-protocol: the official interpreter mediates between the *shallit* (Egyptian-speaking) and the brothers (Hebrew-speaking). The brothers, unaware that Yosef understands Hebrew directly, speak openly to one another in Hebrew at Gen 42:21-22 (their first explicit Gen-37-guilt-confession: *aval ashemim anachnu al achinu* / *dam nidrash*); Yosef overhears the confession directly, and the v 24 weeping follows the v 21-22 overhearing (governed by the SIBLING overlay entry's narrative-architecture observation). terms.translit: kevodi be-Mitzrayim (Gen 45:13 ve-higgadtem le-avi et-kol-kevodi be-Mitzrayim, 'and ye shall tell my father of all my glory in Mitsrayim')

terms.literal: kevodi — my glory / my honor / my prestige / my office-dignity; the Yosef-cycle's court-office-honor register, distinct from the divine-glory cluster
terms.standardEnglish: all my glory (ASV/KJV/NRSV); all my high station (NJPS); all the honor I enjoy (modern, paraphrastic)
terms.wohChoice: all my glory (ASV-baseline preserved; the chapter-specific court-office-honor register documented in commentary; distinguished from the divine-glory-of-YHWH cluster)
terms.rationale: **Gen 45:13 stages Yosef's instruction to the brothers: *ve-higgadtem le-avi et-kol-kevodi be-Mitzrayim ve-et kol-asher re'item* — 'and ye shall tell my father of all my glory in Mitsrayim, and of all that ye have seen'. The noun *kavod* (כָּבוֹד) is deployed here in the senior-court-office-honor register: the *kavod* designates Yosef's office-dignity / prestige / position-of-honor in the Egyptian court. The deployment is distinct from the divine-glory cluster that dominates the lexeme's theological-load-bearing occurrences (Exod 16:7-10; 24:16-17; 33:18-22; 40:34-35; Lev 9:6; Num 14:21; Isa 6:3; Ezek 1:28; 10:18; 43:2-5).** // **The lexeme.** *Kavod* derives from the root *kaved* 'to be heavy, weighty'; the noun's semantic-core is *weight* / *heft* / *substance*. The metaphorical-extensions are extensive: (a) the *honor / dignity / prestige* register (the weight of social-position); (b) the *glory / splendor / magnificence* register (the weight of visible-grandeur); (c) the *divine-glory / kavod YHWH* register (the visible-manifestation of the deity's-presence). The cross-corpus deployment of *kavod* covers all three registers. The Gen 45:13 deployment is in the (a)-(b) zone — the visible-prestige / honor / position-of-the-court-office. // **The court-office-honor register.** The *kavod*-of-court-honor is recognized in cross-corpus contexts: **Esth 1:4** — Achashverosh's court-display: *be-har'oto et-osher kevod malkhuto ve-et-yqar tif'eret gedullato yamim rabim* ('when he shewed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honor of his excellent majesty many days'). **Esth 5:11** — Haman's self-display: *va-yesapper lahem Haman et-kevod oshro ve-rov banav* ('and Haman told them of the glory of his riches, and the multitude of his children'). **Isa 22:18** — the indictment of Shevna: *ve-shamah merkevot kevodkha qlon beit adoneikha* ('and there shall the chariots of thy glory be, thou shame of thy lord's house'). The instruction to report the *kavod* to Ya'aqov is functional: Ya'aqov is to be persuaded that Yosef is alive AND that his position is genuine. The *kavod*-report is the credentialing-narrative the brothers will deliver. The chapter-internal cross-reference to v 27 (the brothers reporting and Ya'aqov's spirit-revival) makes the *kavod*-report functional: the reported court-position is part of what convinces the patriarch. // **Overlay housing.** Chapter-specific court-office-honor deployment. The cross-corpus reach in this specific register is limited (Esth, Isa 22 — both contexts with their own translation-decisions), distinct from the divine-glory cluster which is corpus-saturating. terms.translit: va-yippol al-tzavarav va-yevk (Gen 45:14 va-yippol al-tzav'rei Vinyamin-achiv va-yevk u-Vinyamin bakhah al-tzavarav; Gen 45:15 va-yenashek le-khol-echav va-yevk aleihem)
terms.partOfSpeech: verb-noun construction (Qal of naphal + al-tzavarav prepositional + Qal of bakhah); the corpus's principal reunion-embrace-and-weeping formula
terms.literal: va-yippol al-tzavarav va-yevk — and he fell upon his neck and wept; the embrace-with-weeping formula that the corpus deploys at reunion-moments
terms.standardEnglish: fell upon his neck and wept (ASV/KJV); embraced him and wept (NJPS); fell upon his neck and wept (NRSV); flung himself on his neck and wept (Alter)
terms.wohChoice: fell upon his neck and wept (ASV-baseline preserved; the Genesis-internal reunion-embrace-formula cluster Gen 33:4 + 45:14-15 + 46:29 documented in commentary)
terms.rationale: **Gen 45:14-15 deploys the corpus's principal reunion-embrace-and-weeping formula across two consecutive verses: v 14 (Yosef-Binyamin: *va-yippol al-tzav'rei Vinyamin-achiv va-yevk u-Vinyamin bakhah al-tzavarav*, 'he fell upon his brother Binyamin's neck, and wept; and Binyamin wept upon his neck'); v 15 (Yosef-brothers: *va-yenashek le-khol-echav va-yevk aleihem*, 'and he kissed all his brethren, and wept upon them'). The construction *va-yippol al-tzavarav + va-yevk* ('fell upon his neck and wept') is the corpus's signature reunion-formula. The chapter-internal dual deployment (vv 14, 15) is part of a Genesis-internal triple-deployment cluster: Gen 33:4 (Esav's reunion with Ya'aqov) + Gen 45:14-15 (here) + Gen 46:29 (Yosef's reunion with Ya'aqov).** // **The construction.** The formula combines two action-verbs in characteristic-sequence: (i) *naphal al-tzavarav* — 'to fall on the neck of' — the embrace-action (the falling-upon-the-neck names the active embrace-by-the-elder/larger party, or the mutual-embrace); (ii) *bakhah* — 'to weep' — the emotional-discharge accompanying the embrace. The combination is the corpus's standard reunion-affective-formula: the embrace and the weeping function as a unit, the embrace expressing the recognition-and-reunion physically, the weeping expressing the affective-discharge of long-separation. The Hebrew construction does not specify the embrace's posture precisely (whether arms-around-neck specifically, or chest-to-chest with face-buried-in-neck) — the *naphal al-tzavarav* construction names the embrace-on-the-neck more loosely. The English 'fell upon his neck' (ASV/KJV) preserves the lexical-image; modern translations vary ('embraced him', 'flung himself on his neck'). // **The Genesis-internal reunion-formula cluster.** The construction recurs at three cycle-significant reunion-moments: **(a) Gen 33:4** — Esav's reunion-embrace with Ya'aqov after the Penuel-night: *va-yarotz Esav li-qra'to va-yechabbqehu va-yippol al-tzav'arav va-yishshakehu va-yivku* ('and Esav ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept'). The Gen 33:4 occurrence is the cycle's earlier reunion-embrace; famously marked by the *puncta extraordinaria* over *va-yishshakehu* (the kiss-verb), governed by an existing overlay-entry treating the textual-marker. **(b) Gen 45:14-15 (here)** — Yosef's reunion-embrace with Binyamin and the brothers. The cycle's central disclosure-scene reunion. **(c) Gen 46:29** — Yosef's reunion-embrace with Ya'aqov on the descent: *va-ye'esor Yosef merkavto va-ya'al li-qra't Yisra'el aviv Goshnah va-yera elav va-yippol al-tzavarav va-yevk al-tzavarav od* ('and Yosef made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Yisra'el his father, to Goshen; and he presented himself unto him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while'). The Gen 46:29 occurrence is the cycle's final reunion-embrace (father-son), structurally completing the cycle's reunion-arc. The triple-deployment Gen 33:4 → 45:14-15 → 46:29 is one of the corpus's most-cited reunion-formula clusters (Alter, Sternberg, Sarna). // **The chapter's dual deployment.** The chapter-internal pair at vv 14-15 has a structural-logic: at v 14 the Yosef-Binyamin embrace is mutual and reciprocal (both subjects fall on each other's neck and weep — the only direct-brother of the Rachel-side, the only one Yosef has never had reason to be estranged from); at v 15 the Yosef-brothers embrace is asymmetric (Yosef kisses the brothers and weeps upon them; the brothers do not embrace back — the text records Yosef's outward-affection but the brothers' reciprocity is muted). The contrast — Binyamin reciprocating fully; the other brothers receiving but not (yet) reciprocating — is the chapter's literary signature for the unresolved Gen 37 guilt-residue. Only after Yosef's outward affection does v 15b record *ve-acharei khen dibberu echav itto* ('and after that his brethren talked with him') — speech finally resumes between Yosef and the brothers. // **Overlay housing.** Genesis-internal reunion-embrace-formula cluster (Gen 33:4 + 45:14-15 + 46:29); chapter-specific dual-deployment is the chapter-anchored literary observation. The Gen 33:4 cross-reference is to an existing overlay (governing the puncta extraordinaria, distinct from the embrace-formula). The broader cross-corpus *naphal al-tzavarav* reunion-formula has reach into Luke 15:20 NT (the prodigal-father formula), 2 Kgs 7 + 2 Sam, etc. → **OVERLAY** for the Genesis-internal reunion-formula cluster. // The claim_type is *direct* because (a) the construction is morphologically explicit; (b) the Genesis-internal triple-cluster Gen 33:4 + 45:14-15 + 46:29 is grammatically and textually verifiable; (c) the cross-corpus reunion-formula distribution is documentary; (d) the ASV-baseline 'fell upon his neck and wept' is the direct rendering; (e) the chapter-internal Binyamin-reciprocal / brothers-muted asymmetry is grammatically transparent (the subject-pattern differs between v 14 and v 15). Named scholarship only. // **Scholarly literature.** HALOT s.vv. *naphal*, *tzavar*, *bakhah*; BDB pp. 656-658 (naphal), 848 (tzavar), 113 (bakhah); Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 230 (Gen 33:4), 309-310; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* 1986 pp. 145, 156 (Gen 46:29); Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 pp. 343-344, 579; Alter *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 pp. 264-265; on the Genesis-internal reunion-formula cluster and the literary-architecture of Gen 33:4 / 45:14-15 / 46:29: R. Alter *The Art of Biblical Narrative* 1981 ch. 8; M. Sternberg *The Poetics of Biblical Narrative* 1985 pp. 285-308; J. P. Fokkelman *Narrative Art in Genesis* SSN 17, 1975; on the chapter-internal asymmetry (Binyamin-reciprocal / brothers-muted): G. W. Coats *From Canaan to Egypt* CBQMS 4, 1976.

terms.translit: chelev ha-aretz (Gen 45:18 ve-ikhlu et-chelev ha-aretz, 'and ye shall eat the fat of the land')
terms.partOfSpeech: noun, masculine singular, in the metaphorical 'best/richest part' register; distinct from the technical Levitical sacrificial-fat sense
terms.literal: chelev ha-aretz — the fat of the land / the best of the land / the richest portion of the land's produce; the metaphorical-extension of the chelev-fat noun
terms.standardEnglish: the fat of the land (ASV/KJV/NRSV); the best of the land (NJPS); the richness of the land (modern)
terms.wohChoice: the fat of the land (ASV-baseline preserved; the metaphorical 'best-of-the-land' sense and the distinction from the Levitical sacrificial-fat prohibition-register documented in commentary)
terms.rationale: **Gen 45:18 deploys the noun *chelev* in the Pharaoh-grant idiom *chelev ha-aretz* ('the fat of the land'): Pharaoh's pledge to Yosef's family of *tuv eretz Mitzrayim* and *chelev ha-aretz* ('I will give you the good of the land of Mitsrayim, and ye shall eat the fat of the land'). The construction deploys *chelev* in its metaphorical 'best/richest part' register, distinct from the technical Levitical sacrificial-fat sense (Lev 3:14-17; 7:23-25 — the prohibition on eating the suet/visceral-fat of sacrificial animals). The metaphorical-extension is well-attested across the corpus's poetic and didactic literature.** // **The two registers of *chelev*.** The noun *chelev* (חֵלֶב) covers two distinct semantic-registers: **(a) the literal sacrificial-fat sense** — the visceral suet of sacrificial animals, used in the technical Levitical / sacrificial vocabulary. The Levitical-Code's prohibition is precise: *kol chelev ve-khol dam lo tochelu* ('ye shall eat neither fat nor blood', Lev 3:17; 7:23-25). The literal-fat is restricted from human consumption in the H-Code. **(b) the metaphorical 'best/richest part' sense** — the lexical-extension to mean 'the best portion', 'the richest yield', 'the choicest of'. The metaphor derives from the agricultural-ethnographic context: the suet/visceral-fat is the densest-and-richest part of the animal; by extension, the *chelev* of anything is its richest-or-densest-portion. The metaphorical-extension is widely-attested across the corpus's poetic and didactic literature. The two registers are contextually-distinguishable: the technical-fat occurrences are in the Levitical-and-cultic contexts; the metaphorical occurrences are in the agricultural-blessing, the poetic, and the didactic contexts. The Gen 45:18 occurrence is unambiguously in register (b). // **The metaphorical 'best-of-the-land' cross-corpus distribution.** The construction *chelev* + (genitive-of-the-thing) is the standard formula for the metaphorical 'best/richest part of'. The principal attestations: **Num 18:12** — the priestly grant from the people: *kol chelev yitzhar ve-khol chelev tirosh ve-dagan reishitam asher-yittnu la-YHWH lekha netattim* ('all the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine, and of the wheat, the firstfruits of them which they offer unto YHWH, them have I given thee'). The Num 18:12 deployment names the priestly portions as the *chelev* (best part) of the oil + wine + grain. **Deut 32:14** — the Song of Mosheh, Israel-as-blessed: *chem'at baqar va-chalev tzon im-chelev karim ve-eilim... ve-dam-enav tishteh-chamer* ('butter of kine, and milk of sheep, with fat of lambs, and rams... and of the blood of the grape thou didst drink wine'). The Song of Mosheh deploys *chelev* twice — first literally (the fat of the lambs), second metaphorically (the *chelev* of wheat-and-other-produce in the surrounding verses). **Ps 81:17 [MT 81:17]** — the divine speech of providence: *va-ya'akhilehu me-chelev chittah u-mi-tzur d'vash asbi'eka* ('he would have fed them also with the fat of wheat: and with honey out of the rock should I have satisfied thee'). The metaphorical *chelev chittah* names the best-of-the-wheat. **Ps 147:14** — *ha-sam g'vulech shalom chelev chittim yasbi'ekh* ('he maketh peace in thy borders, and filleth thee with the finest of the wheat'). The metaphorical 'finest of the wheat' Psalmic-formula. The cross-corpus deployment is therefore well-established. // **The Pharaoh-grant context.** Pharaoh's pledge at Gen 45:18 is in the deferential-magnificence register: the gift to the *shallit*-Yosef-and-his-family is the *tuv* + *chelev* of Mitsrayim — both 'the good of the land' and 'the fat of the land'. The construction is the corpus's only deployment of the *chelev ha-aretz* phrase in this specific register (the other metaphorical-*chelev* deployments specify the agricultural-product: *chelev chittah* / *chelev yitzhar* / *chelev karim*; here the unspecified *chelev ha-aretz* covers the whole-of-the-land's-bounty). The Pharaoh-grant rhetorical force: the most generous expression of Egyptian-court hospitality, the offer of the kingdom's choicest-resources. The literary point (Sarna): Pharaoh's offer is one of the cycle's three most-magnificent court-grants (alongside Yosef's investiture at Gen 41:42-45 and the post-Ya'aqov-death honor at Gen 50:7-9). // **Overlay housing.** Chapter-specific Pharaoh-grant deployment; the cross-corpus metaphorical *chelev*-distribution (Num 18:12, Deut 32:14, Ps 81:17, 147:14) is documented but the chapter-specific *chelev ha-aretz* unspecified-construction is here. The broader metaphorical-*chelev* lexeme is noted as a promotion-seed for the eventual Numbers / Deuteronomy / Psalter translations. → **OVERLAY** with promotion-seed noted. // The claim_type is *direct* because (a) the noun is morphologically explicit; (b) the metaphorical 'best-of-the-land' sense is grammatically and contextually transparent; (c) the cross-corpus distribution of the metaphorical-extension is verifiable; (d) the distinction from the Levitical sacrificial-fat prohibition-register is established across the standard lexica; (e) the ASV-baseline 'the fat of the land' is the direct rendering. Named scholarship only. // **Scholarly literature.** HALOT s.v. *chelev*; BDB pp. 316-317; TDOT IV:391-397; NIDOTTE 2:139-141; Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 310; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* 1986 p. 145; Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 p. 580; on the metaphorical *chelev*-extension: M. Greenberg 'Cult' EncJud; on the Levitical sacrificial-fat prohibition: J. Milgrom *Leviticus 1-16* AB 1991 pp. 205-211; on the Ps 81:17 / 147:14 Psalmic-deployment: H.-J. Kraus *Psalms 1-59* + *Psalms 60-150* CC 1988-89.

terms.translit: agalot (Gen 45:19 va-yiqachu agalot; Gen 45:21 va-yitten lahem Yosef agalot; Gen 45:27 va-yare et-ha-agalot asher-shalach Yosef)
terms.partOfSpeech: noun, feminine plural (singular agalah); the wheeled-vehicle / cart / wagon designation, distinct from the chariot lexemes (merkavah, rekhev)
terms.literal: agalot — wagons / carts / wheeled-vehicles for transport-of-persons-and-goods; the cycle's three-fold deployment for the Pharaoh-issue family-transport vehicles
terms.standardEnglish: wagons (ASV/KJV/NRSV/NJPS — uncontested)
terms.wohChoice: wagons (ASV-baseline preserved; the chapter's three-fold deployment for the Pharaoh-issue family-transport vehicles and the Egyptological apparatus documented in commentary)
terms.rationale: **Genesis 45 deploys *agalot* ('wagons') three times — at v 19 (Pharaoh's instruction: *qechu lakhem me-eretz Mitzrayim agalot le-tappkhem ve-li-nsheikhem*, 'take you wagons out of the land of Mitsrayim for your little ones, and for your wives'); v 21 (the fulfilment: *va-yitten lahem Yosef agalot al-pi Far'oh*, 'Yosef gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh'); v 27 (Ya'aqov's seeing the wagons as the credentialing-confirmation: *va-yare et-ha-agalot asher-shalach Yosef la-set oto va-techi ruach Ya'aqov*, 'when he saw the wagons which Yosef had sent to carry him, the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived'). The chapter's three-fold *agalah*-deployment is structurally significant: the wagons are the chapter's material-token of Pharaoh's hospitality and Yosef's sustenance-promise, and at v 27 the wagons function as the empirical-proof that turns Ya'aqov from disbelief (v 26 *va-yafag libbo*) to revival (v 27 *va-techi ruach*).** // **The lexeme.** *Agalah* (עֲגָלָה) is the standard HB designation for the wheeled-vehicle / cart / wagon. The lexeme is distinguished from the chariot-vocabulary (*merkavah*, *rekhev*) by its function: the *agalah* is a transport-vehicle (for persons and goods, drawn by oxen or other draft-animals); the *merkavah* is the military / royal-display chariot (typically drawn by horses, with a war-or-ceremonial function). The etymological root is debated (possibly from *agal* 'to roll, be round' — naming the wheel; possibly from *agol* 'round/circular' — naming the form). The lexeme's principal cross-corpus deployments: // **(1) The Mishkan-transport (Num 7:3 + 6-8).** The tribal-leaders' offerings include *shesh eglot tzav u-shnei-asar baqar* ('six covered wagons, and twelve oxen'), distributed to the Levite-clans for the transport of the Mishkan's components. The Num 7 deployment names the wagons as cultic-transport vehicles. // **(2) The Pelishtim's ark-return (1 Sam 6:7-14).** The Pelishtim construct a *agalah chadashah* ('a new wagon') for the return-of-the-ark; the wagon-and-cows divinatory-test functions as the chapter's principal narrative-device. The 1 Sam 6 deployment names the wagon as the ark-transport vehicle in the Pelishtim context. // **(3) Uzzah's ill-fated ark-transport (2 Sam 6:3).** David's first attempt to bring the ark to Yerushalayim uses *agalah chadashah* ('a new wagon'); Uzzah's death-by-divine-strike at the threshing-floor of Nakhon is the chapter's narrative-pivot. The 2 Sam 6 deployment names the wagon as the ark-transport vehicle in the early-monarchic context. // **(4) Prophetic / wisdom deployment.** **Isa 5:18** (the cart-rope idiom: *hoy moshkhei he-avon be-chablei ha-shav ve-kha'avot ha-agalah chatta'ah*, 'woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope'); **Amos 2:13** (*hinneh anokhi me'iq tachteikhem ka-asher ta'iq ha-agalah ha-melea'h lah amir*, 'behold, I will press you, as a cart full of sheaves presseth'). The prophetic-poetic deployments use the *agalah* in agricultural-burden-bearing imagery. // **The Egyptological apparatus.** Egyptological evidence for the New Kingdom royal-issue wagons is documented: the Egyptian state under the Eighteenth and Nineteenth Dynasties maintained a corps of wheeled-vehicles for state-transport-of-persons-and-goods; the wagons could be issued from royal storehouses for diplomatic / family / agricultural purposes. The biblical-Pharaoh's gift of *agalot* at Gen 45:19 + 21 is therefore historically-plausible Egyptian-court practice. The Egyptological scholarship: P. Vergote *Joseph en Égypte* OBL 3, 1959 pp. 173-181 (the wagon-and-chariot transport practice); D. B. Redford *A Study of the Biblical Story of Joseph* VTSup 20, 1970; K. A. Kitchen *Reliability of the Old Testament* 2003. The Egyptological documentation is presented as historical-context, not as adjudication of the narrative's historical-veracity. // **The chapter's narrative-function.** The wagons serve as the chapter's material-proof of Yosef's status and Pharaoh's hospitality. At v 19 + 21 the wagons are the Pharaoh-grant; at v 27 the wagons are the visual-confirmation that turns Ya'aqov from disbelief to revival. The narrative-architecture is precise: Ya'aqov disbelieves the brothers' verbal-report (*lo-he'emin lahem*, v 26b) until he sees the wagons-as-physical-evidence (*va-yare et-ha-agalot*, v 27). The wagons are the chapter's principal credentialing-token; the lexical-repetition across vv 19, 21, 27 anchors the narrative-arc from Pharaoh's grant through Ya'aqov's seeing. // **Overlay housing.** Cycle-internal chapter-anchor; the cross-corpus deployment (Num 7, 1 Sam 6, 2 Sam 6, Isa 5, Amos 2) is documentary but the cycle-specific chapter-45-to-46 transition deployment is here. → **OVERLAY** with promotion-seed noted for the eventual Numbers / Samuel translations. // The claim_type is *direct* because (a) the noun is morphologically explicit; (b) the chapter's three-fold deployment is grammatically and textually transparent; (c) the cross-corpus distribution is verifiable; (d) the ASV-baseline 'wagons' is the consensus rendering; (e) the Egyptological context is documentary. terms.standardEnglish: five changes of raiment (ASV/KJV); five changes of clothing (NJPS); five changes of garments (Alter)

terms.rationale: **Gen 45:22 stages the cycle's five-fold gift to Binyamin: *u-le-Vinyamin natan shelosh me'ot kesef ve-chamesh chalifot semalot* ('but to Binyamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver, and five changes of raiment'). The cycle's fives-pattern across the broader cycle: Gen 41:34 (*chimmesh*, the Piel administrative-verb governed by the existing overlay [`chimmesh-fifth-part-or-fifth-division-gen41`](#chimmesh-fifth-part-or-fifth-division-gen41)); Gen 43:34 (*chamesh yadot*, the fivefold-portion governed by the existing overlay [`chamesh-yadot-fivefold-portion-gen43`](#chamesh-yadot-fivefold-portion-gen43)); Gen 45:6, 11, 22 (here); Gen 47:2 (*chamesh anashim*, the five brothers Yosef presents to Pharaoh). terms.translit: al-tirgezu ba-derekh (Gen 45:24 va-yomer aleihem al-tirgezu ba-derekh, 'and he said unto them, see that ye fall not out by the way')
terms.partOfSpeech: verb, Qal imperfect 2mp; the ragaz lexeme's wide semantic-range produces a recognized philological crux
terms.literal: al-tirgezu ba-derekh — be not [verb-range: tremble / be-agitated / be-anxious / quarrel / argue] on the way; Yosef's farewell-instruction to the brothers as they depart
terms.standardEnglish: see that ye fall not out by the way (ASV/KJV — the quarrel-reading); do not be quarrelsome (NJPS, similar); do not be troubled along the way (Alter, the anxious-reading)
terms.wohChoice: see that ye fall not out by the way (ASV-baseline preserved; the four-reading philological crux documented in commentary; the quarrel-reading is the dominant Jewish-tradition + KJV/ASV consensus)
terms.rationale: **Gen 45:24 closes the chapter's disclosure-and-departure scene with Yosef's marked farewell-instruction: *va-yshallach et-echav va-yelekhu va-yomer aleihem al-tirgezu ba-derekh* — 'so he sent his brethren away, and they departed: and he said unto them, see that ye fall not out by the way'. The verb *ragaz* carries an unusually wide semantic-range that produces a recognized philological crux, with significant interpretive traditions divided across four principal readings. The crux has been treated as a tannaitic / rabbinic / medieval interpretation-problem from at least the 3rd-century-CE tradition.** // **The four-reading polysemy of *ragaz*.** The verb *ragaz* (רגז) covers a semantic-range broader than any single English-rendering can capture: (i) the dominant 'tremble / be agitated / be in turmoil' sense — the standard physical-or-emotional-agitation register (Exod 15:14 *ragzu yoshvei Pelashet*, 'the inhabitants of Pelashet shall tremble'; Deut 2:25 *ha-amim... yirgezu mi-paneikha*; 1 Sam 14:15 *va-tehi charadat machaneh ba-sadeh... va-yirgezu ha-aretz*; 1 Sam 28:5; 2 Sam 7:10 = 1 Chr 17:9; Isa 5:25 + 14:9 + 23:11; Ezek 16:43; Mic 7:17; Hab 3:7); (ii) the affective 'be moved with emotion / be disturbed / be anxious' sense — the emotional-disturbance register (2 Sam 19:1 [MT 19:1] *va-yirgaz ha-melekh*, David's grief over Avshalom; Ps 4:5 *rigzu ve-al techeta'u*, 'be moved/troubled and sin not'); (iii) the conflict 'quarrel, dispute, contend with one another' sense — the rabbinic-tradition reading; (iv) the fear 'be afraid' sense — the affective-fear register (some occurrences). // **The rabbinic and Jewish-tradition reading.** The Jewish interpretive tradition predominantly reads the verse in the conflict / quarrel sense. **b. Ta'anit 10b** records an attributed-reading to R. Eleazar: *shelo titasqu bi-dvar halakhah she-mma yargizu aleichem ha-derekh* ('do not occupy yourselves with halakhic dispute, lest the way become turbulent against you'). **Rashi** on Gen 45:24 cites multiple readings: (a) *al tariv* — 'do not quarrel' — the primary tradition; (b) *al tifsa pesi'ah gasah* — 'do not take a wide stride' (a tradition that the brothers should not journey-too-quickly); (c) *al ta'amidu et atzmichem ba-derekh mi-dvar halakhah* — 'do not stop on the way to debate halakhah' (combining the quarrel-reading with the b. Ta'anit reading). **Targum Onqelos** renders the verse with *la-titnatzun be-orcha* ('do not contend on the road'), preserving the quarrel-reading. **Sa'adia Gaon** renders with the fear-reading 'do not be alarmed'. The dominant Jewish-tradition reading is therefore the quarrel-or-contention reading; the KJV/ASV 'see that ye fall not out by the way' preserves this tradition. // **The modern critical readings.** Modern critical translations vary: NJPS 'do not be quarrelsome' (the quarrel-reading); Alter 'do not be troubled along the way' (the anxious / disturbed reading); modern functional translations sometimes offer 'do not argue', 'do not be agitated', 'do not be anxious'. The modern lexica (HALOT, BDB, TDOT) document the verb's wide semantic-range without adjudicating the Gen 45:24 deployment specifically. // **The interpretive context.** The chapter's narrative-context provides some constraints: (a) the brothers have just been verbally-acknowledged-by-Yosef as the ones who sold him (v 4-5); the journey-back-to-Ya'aqov is an emotionally-charged occasion (they must report to the father whose grief over Yosef has lasted twenty-two years); (b) the brothers' moral-arc has been one of guilt-and-confession (Gen 42:21; 44:16); the question of WHICH brother is most-responsible for the original sale (Yehudah proposed; Re'uven dissented; the brothers executed) could plausibly produce quarrels-among-themselves on the journey; (c) Pharaoh's grant has just been received — the new wealth and the new prospect of resettlement could plausibly produce dispute-over-the-distribution. The contextual-considerations support the quarrel-reading without ruling out the agitation / anxiety reading. The ASV-baseline 'fall not out by the way' preserves the quarrel-reading-tradition. // **Overlay housing.** Chapter-specific Yosef-instruction; the wider *ragaz*-lexeme has corpus-saturating distribution but the chapter-specific philological crux is here. → **OVERLAY** as a chapter-singular philological-and-rabbinic crux. // The claim_type is *inferred* because (a) the lexeme is morphologically explicit (Qal of *ragaz*) but the specific-sense at Gen 45:24 is contested across the named-tradition readings; (b) the polysemy is documented across the standard lexica; (c) the rabbinic tradition's quarrel-reading is documented in named scholarship (b. Ta'an. 10b, Rashi); (d) the modern critical readings vary; (e) the ASV-baseline preserves the quarrel-reading (the dominant Jewish-tradition + KJV/ASV consensus). The choice among the readings is interpretive, hence inferred. Named scholarship only; no project synthesis. // **Scholarly literature.** HALOT s.v. *ragaz*; BDB p. 919; TDOT XIII:312-318; NIDOTTE 3:1052-1055; Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 311; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* 1986 p. 146; Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 p. 581; Alter *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 265; on the rabbinic tradition and Rashi's multiple-readings: M. Rosenbaum and A. M. Silbermann *Pentateuch with Targum Onkelos, Haphtaroth and Rashi's Commentary* 1929-34 (Genesis); on the b. Ta'an. 10b reading: J. Neusner *The Talmud of Babylonia: An American Translation* (Ta'anit); on Targum Onqelos: M. McNamara *Targum and Testament Revisited* 2010; on the modern critical readings: E. A. Speiser *AB Genesis* 1964 pp. 339-340.

terms.translit: va-yafag libbo (Gen 45:26 ki lo-he'emin lahem va-yafag libbo, 'and his heart fainted, for he believed them not')
terms.partOfSpeech: verb, Qal imperfect 3ms (here in the rare Qal-stem deployment of pug 'grow numb, faint, cease, become feeble') + libbo 'his heart' as subject
terms.literal: va-yafag libbo — and his heart grew-numb / fainted / ceased / became feeble; the rare Qal-form for emotional-physiological collapse
terms.standardEnglish: his heart fainted (ASV/KJV); his heart went numb (NJPS); his heart went out (modern, paraphrastic); his heart stopped (functional)
terms.wohChoice: his heart fainted (ASV-baseline preserved; the rare Qal-form's chapter-singular hapax status within Genesis and the Ps 77:3 + Hab 1:4 cross-corpus parallels documented in commentary)
terms.rationale: **Gen 45:26 stages Ya'aqov's response to the brothers' impossible news: *va-yagiddu lo lemor od Yosef chai ve-khi-hu moshel be-khol eretz Mitzrayim va-yafag libbo ki lo-he'emin lahem* — 'and they told him, saying, Yosef is yet alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Mitsrayim. And his heart fainted, for he believed them not'. The construction *va-yafag libbo* deploys the rare Qal of *pug* 'grow numb, faint, cease, become feeble' with the heart as subject. The lexeme is extremely rare: the *va-yafag libbo* construction is hapax within Genesis and near-singular within the HB. The chapter's emotional-collapse marker for Ya'aqov's disbelief stands in deliberate contrast to v 27's *va-techi ruach Ya'aqov* (the spirit-revival on seeing the wagons).** // **The lexeme.** *Pug* (פוג) is a rare HB lexeme with a small distribution. The principal occurrences: (i) **Gen 45:26 (here)** — the Qal *va-yafag libbo* — Ya'aqov's heart-numbing on the impossible news. (ii) **Ps 77:3 [MT 77:3]** — the de profundis lament: *be-yom tzarati Adonai darashti yadi laylah niggrah ve-lo tafug, me'anah hinnachem nafshi* ('in the day of my trouble I sought the Lord: my hand was stretched out in the night, and ceased not / and did not grow-numb; my soul refused to be comforted'). The Ps 77:3 deployment uses the Qal-stem in the related parallel-stich with negation (*ve-lo tafug*, 'did not cease / grow-numb'); the lexeme names the not-ceasing of the lament-hand. (iii) **Hab 1:4** — the prophet's complaint: *al-ken tafug torah ve-lo-yetze la-netzach mishpat* ('therefore the law is slacked / grown-feeble, and judgment doth never go forth'). The Hab 1:4 deployment uses the Hiphil-stem (the standard form-analysis treats *tafug* here as Qal third-person-feminine-singular though some grammars register Hiphil; the cessation / weakening sense is shared). The lexeme's distribution is therefore extremely-limited: Gen 45:26 + Ps 77:3 + Hab 1:4 (with debated form-analysis). The Gen 45:26 construction is the lexeme's signature deployment for emotional-physiological collapse. // **The semantic-core.** The lexeme's core sense is *cessation / numbing / weakening*: the action being-performed ceases-or-grows-feeble. The Gen 45:26 deployment names the heart's-ceasing in the affective sense — Ya'aqov's heart 'fainted', i.e., the normal-functioning of the heart's affective-and-cognitive capacities was momentarily suspended in the shock. The construction is psycho-physical: the heart in HB anthropology is the seat of cognition + affect + decision (not just the affective-organ as in modern Western anthropology); the heart's *faging* (numbing) names the comprehensive-shutdown of the cognitive-affective center. The English 'fainted' (ASV) preserves the physiological-emotional collapse sense; modern 'went numb' (NJPS) modernizes; functional 'stopped' captures the cessation-aspect. // **The chapter's emotional arc.** The Gen 45:26 deployment is the chapter's emotional-pivot for Ya'aqov, structurally paired with the immediately-following v 27 *va-techi ruach Ya'aqov avihem* ('the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived'). The arc: at v 26 the heart-faints (the disbelief-shock); at v 27a the brothers continue to report (*va-yedabbru elav et kol-divrei Yosef asher dibber aleihem*) and Ya'aqov sees the wagons (*va-yare et-ha-agalot*); at v 27b the spirit-revives. The lexical pairing *va-yafag libbo* (v 26) / *va-techi ruach* (v 27) maps the affective-physiological collapse / revival across the two-verse pivot. The literary point (Alter, Sternberg, Sarna): the chapter's chayah-arc (v 5 *le-michyah* / v 7 *u-le-hachayot* / v 27 *va-techi ruach*) closes here by tracing the providential-purpose all the way to the patriarch's literal revival. // **Overlay housing.** Chapter-singular within Genesis (the only Genesis occurrence); near-hapax within the HB (the Ps 77:3 and Hab 1:4 parallels are the only cross-corpus occurrences). The chapter-specific emotional-collapse marker is the chapter-anchored literary observation. → **OVERLAY** as a chapter-singular hapax-form. // The claim_type is *direct* because (a) the verb is morphologically explicit (Qal of *pug*); (b) the chapter-singular hapax-status is verifiable; (c) the Ps 77:3 + Hab 1:4 cross-corpus parallels are documented; (d) the ASV-baseline 'his heart fainted' is the direct rendering. Named scholarship only. // **Scholarly literature.** HALOT s.v. *pug*; BDB p. 806; TDOT XI:545-547; NIDOTTE 3:602-604; Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 311; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* 1986 p. 147; Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 p. 582; Alter *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 265; on the chapter's chayah-arc and the v 26 / v 27 affective-pivot: M. Sternberg *The Poetics of Biblical Narrative* 1985 pp. 285-308; R. Alter *The Art of Biblical Narrative* 1981 ch. 8; on Ps 77:3: H.-J. Kraus *Psalms 60-150* CC 1989; on Hab 1:4: J. J. M. Roberts *Nahum, Habakkuk, and Zephaniah* OTL 1991.

terms.translit: va-techi ruach Ya'aqov (Gen 45:27 va-techi ruach Ya'aqov avihem, 'the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived')
terms.partOfSpeech: verb-noun construction; the Qal of chayah in the figurative 'revive / be brought back to life' sense with the noun ruach as subject
terms.literal: va-techi ruach Ya'aqov — the spirit of Ya'aqov lived / revived / returned-to-life; the spirit-revival idiom for emotional-physiological restoration
terms.standardEnglish: the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived (ASV/KJV); the spirit of their father Ya'aqov came back to life (NJPS); the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived (NRSV)
terms.wohChoice: the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived (ASV-baseline preserved; the chayah-of-spirit-revival construction and the chapter's chayah-keyword arc closure documented in commentary; sibling-link to the central `michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun`)
terms.rationale:
**Gen 45:27 stages the chapter's closing affective-pivot: *va-yedabbru elav et kol-divrei Yosef asher dibber alehem va-yare et-ha-agalot asher-shalach Yosef la-set oto va-techi ruach Ya'aqov avihem* — 'and they told him all the words of Yosef, which he had said unto them: and when he saw the wagons which Yosef had sent to carry him, the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived'. The construction *va-techi ruach Ya'aqov* deploys the Qal of *chayah* ('to live') in the figurative 'revive / be brought back to life' sense, with the noun *ruach* ('spirit / breath') as subject. The chapter-internal cross-occurrences explicit echo: v 5 *le-michyah* (the providential-purpose noun, governed by the SIBLING central [`michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun`](#michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun)); v 7 *u-le-hachayot* (the expanded-providential-purpose Hiphil-infinitive); v 27 *va-techi ruach Ya'aqov* (the chapter-closing fulfilment, here). The chapter's chayah-keyword arc — providential-purpose (v 5) → expanded-purpose (v 7) → fulfilment-in-the-father's-spirit-revival (v 27) — is one of the chapter's structural literary signatures.** // **The construction.** The Hebrew *chayah* (Qal) is the standard 'to live' verb; the figurative-extension to the 'revive / come-back-to-life' sense is well-attested. The construction *va-techi ruach* + (person)'s-spirit deploys the verb with *ruach* ('spirit / breath / animating-principle') as the subject — the spirit-revives, the spirit-comes-back-to-life. The construction's psycho-physical force: in HB anthropology the *ruach* is the animating-principle that distinguishes the living-from-the-dead (Gen 2:7 *nishmat chayyim*); the *ruach*'s revival names the comprehensive-restoration of the human's vitality. The Gen 45:27 deployment names Ya'aqov's revival from the *va-yafag libbo* of v 26: the heart that had fainted now has its spirit revive. The narrative-architecture is precise: the patriarch moves from disbelief-and-collapse (v 26) to belief-and-revival (v 27) via the visual-evidence of the wagons. // **The cross-corpus chayah-of-spirit-revival construction.** The construction recurs at structurally-significant moments across the corpus: **Judg 15:19** — Shimshon's well at Lechi: *va-tashav rucho va-yechi* ('his spirit came back, and he revived') — the spirit-returns / he-lives formula, after Shimshon's thirst-near-death-and-divine-water. **1 Sam 30:12** — the Mitsri-servant David finds in the desert: *va-tashav rucho elav ki lo-akhal lechem ve-lo-shatah mayim sheloshet yamim u-shloshet leilot* ('and when he had eaten, his spirit came again to him: for he had eaten no bread, nor drunk any water, three days and three nights'). The 1 Sam 30:12 deployment uses the same spirit-returns-revival formula. The cross-corpus deployment establishes the construction as the corpus's standard spirit-revival formula for restoration from physical-or-emotional collapse. // **The chapter-internal chayah-keyword arc.** The chapter's chayah-vocabulary arc is one of its principal literary structures. The arc traces: (a) v 5 — *ki le-michyah shelachani Elohim lifneikhem* (providential-sending-purpose: 'for preservation-of-life Elohim sent me before you'); (b) v 7 — *va-yishlacheni Elohim lifneikhem la-sum lakhem she'erit ba-aretz u-le-hachayot lakhem li-pleitah gedolah* (expanded-providential-purpose: 'and Elohim sent me before you to preserve you a remnant in the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance'); (c) v 27 — *va-techi ruach Ya'aqov avihem* (chapter-closing fulfilment: 'the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived'). The arc's literary architecture: the providential-sending's purpose is preservation-of-life (v 5); the purpose is expanded to cover the remnant's preservation (v 7); the purpose is fulfilled at the chapter's close in the literal-revival of the patriarch's spirit (v 27). The chapter's structure is therefore precisely a chayah-narrative: the preservation-of-life-as-providential-purpose tracks all the way to the father's literal revival. The literary point (Alter, Westermann, Sarna): the chayah-arc is one of the chapter's most-significant unifying structures. // **Bidirectional sibling-link to the central `michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun`.** The chapter's chayah-keyword arc is governed at the v 5 end by the SIBLING central entry [`michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun`](#michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun) (the rare *michyah* noun naming the providential-purpose) and the SIBLING central [`shelachani-elohim-lifneikhem-providential-sending-formula-yosef-cycle`](#shelachani-elohim-lifneikhem-providential-sending-formula-yosef-cycle) (the providential-sending formula). The v 27 closure is governed by this overlay entry. The three entries jointly track the chapter's chayah-arc: the central-pair at v 5 (the providential-purpose), the overlay entry here at v 27 (the chapter-closing fulfilment). The central-overlay sibling-link is bidirectional: this entry names the central sibling by id; the central sibling's rationale documents the chapter-internal chayah-keyword arc (vv 5, 7, 27). // **Overlay housing.** Chapter-anchored chayah-keyword arc closure; the chayah-of-spirit-revival construction is documented; cross-corpus parallels (Judg 15:19, 1 Sam 30:12) noted. → **OVERLAY** as the chapter-internal arc-closure with central-overlay sibling-link. // The claim_type is *direct* because (a) the construction is morphologically explicit (Qal of *chayah* + *ruach* subject); (b) the chapter-internal chayah-arc (vv 5, 7, 27) is grammatically and textually transparent; (c) the cross-corpus spirit-revival parallels (Judg 15:19, 1 Sam 30:12) are documented; (d) the ASV-baseline 'the spirit of Ya'aqov their father revived' is the direct rendering. Named scholarship only. // **Scholarly literature.** HALOT s.v. *chayah* (Qal), *ruach*; BDB pp. 310-311 (chayah), 924-926 (ruach); TDOT IV:324-344 (chayah), XIII:365-396 (ruach); NIDOTTE 2:108-117; Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 311; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* 1986 p. 147; Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 p. 583; Alter *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 265; on the chapter's chayah-arc: R. Alter *The Art of Biblical Narrative* 1981 ch. 8; M. Sternberg *The Poetics of Biblical Narrative* 1985 pp. 285-308; on Judg 15:19 the Shimshon-revival: J. A. Soggin *Judges* OTL 1981; on 1 Sam 30:12 the Mitsri-servant: P. K. McCarter *1 Samuel* AB 1980.

**Cross-reference (the Gen 46:30 *amutah ha-pa'am* sibling-overlay link).** The chapter-45 chayah-arc closure at v 27 finds its cycle-pair at Gen 46:30: Ya'aqov's *amutah ha-pa'am* ('now let me die'). The Gen 45:28 *od Yosef beni chai elkhah ve-er'ennu be-terem amut* ('I will go and see him before I die') / Gen 46:30 *amutah ha-pa'am acharei re'oti et-paneikha ki odkha chai* ('now let me die, since I have seen thy face, that thou art yet alive') is one of the cycle's structurally-paired death-readiness statements. The Gen 46:30 statement is governed by the sibling overlay-entry [`amutah-ha-paam-death-readiness-yaaqov-gen46`](#amutah-ha-paam-death-readiness-yaaqov-gen46); the bidirectional cross-reference jointly tracks the cycle's death-readiness arc closure across the chapters.
